document.title: MOED Comprehensive User Manual
document.subject: Illustrated application reference, version 2.4.19, updated October 5, 2026

manual-topic-orientation-getting-oriente.title: Getting Oriented
manual-topic-orientation-getting-oriente.text: MOED keeps event planning, people, communication history, and next actions connected instead of scattering them across separate systems. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Daily dashboard (p. 13) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-orientation-the-record-mode.title: The Record Model at a Glance
manual-topic-orientation-the-record-mode.text: An Inquiry holds a possible booking while it is being qualified. Once booked, it creates an Engagement linked to an Organization and its Contacts. These records can carry Chron Log history and Follow-Up Work.

manual-topic-orientation-use-the-sidebar.title: Use the Sidebar
manual-topic-orientation-use-the-sidebar.text: The logo stays at the top of the sidebar and your profile and sign-out controls stay at the bottom. Scroll the menu between them to reach every destination. Under Work, open Email Templates; under Schedule, open Calendar. Administrators also have Network under Administration. On a narrow screen, use the menu button in the top bar. The drawer keeps its logo, close button, and account controls visible while the menu scrolls. Select Close navigation, tap outside the panel, or press Esc to close it.

manual-topic-orientation-switch-the-them.title: Switch the Theme
manual-topic-orientation-switch-the-them.text: Select Dark Theme or Light Theme near the bottom of the sidebar. MOED remembers the choice in this browser.

manual-topic-orientation-open-your-accou.title: Open Your Account
manual-topic-orientation-open-your-accou.text: Select your fixed name and picture block to edit your profile, or its adjacent sign-out icon to log out. Account Security, User Manual, Mattermost, and the theme switch are in the lower part of the scrollable menu.

manual-topic-orientation-a-practical-fir.title: A Practical First Session
manual-topic-orientation-a-practical-fir.text: 01 Complete your profile. Review your name, phone, picture, and verified recovery email in My Profile. 02 Protect the account. Enroll an authenticator and store the one-time recovery codes from Account Security. 03 Check the daily view. Use the Dashboard to scan upcoming engagements, assigned work, and missing details. 04 Find the relationship. Open the organization and relevant contacts before an event to review relationship details, financial history, Chron, and open work. 05 Leave a clear next action. When a conversation creates a commitment, record the communication in Chron and create an owned, dated task.

manual-topic-orientation-learn-with-ai-c.title: Learn with AI Coach
manual-topic-orientation-learn-with-ai-c.text: When enabled for your installation, ai coach helps you understand MOED and learn how to use its controls. Select the ai coach button on a signed-in application page, or Learn with ai coach at the top of this manual. On a wide screen the panel sits beside the page in the right margin; on a narrower screen it opens over the page. Use the minus button to minimize it and the ai coach button to reopen it. 01 Ask about your goal. Type in How do I…?, then press Enter or select Ask. For example, ask "What does MOED do?" or "How do I add speaker notes to this presentation?" Use Shift+Enter for a new line. 02 Follow the explanation or guided step. The coach uses your current page, role, and basic interface state to guide you. It can explain a feature conversationally, give numbered instructions, or offer a supported interactive walkthrough. A follow-up question can refer to the preceding conversation. 03 Check the source and make the change yourself. Manual source buttons open the relevant page of the Comprehensive User Guide PDF. The coach draws on this guide and verified application procedures. It does not enter field values, upload a file, save a form, send a message, or grant additional permissions. The conversation and walkthrough cards appear in chronological order. Sending a question brings the latest question and answer into view. You can navigate to another MOED page in the same browser tab while an answer is being prepared; the panel resumes the conversation there.

manual-topic-orientation-follow-an-inter.title: Follow an Interactive Walkthrough
manual-topic-orientation-follow-an-inter.text: The opening panel offers eight walkthroughs: add a new event, add speaker notes pdf, add a powerpoint, understand waiting tasks, add a task, assign a task, change event dates, and subscribe to your calendar. Ask in your own words or select an option. Questions about why a feature works receive explanations; an unclear task may need one clarifying question before steps are offered. For event tasks, select the event's Tasks tab before Add Task. In a task form, use Change record and Find a related record to choose a different linked record. Assignment uses Assigned to; the check-mark completes a task. Calendar subscriptions are personal and available to reviewers too. The copy step appears only after the private link has been created; keep that link out of coach questions. 01 Choose the task. The card starts from your current page. If the task needs another page, use its navigation link. For a new event, go to Engagements, select + New Engagement, and choose the organization inside the form. 02 Locate the next control. Select the card's show button to highlight the named control. You still select it yourself. For presentation files, first select the event's Presentations tab, then Edit Presentations; the editing button is not visible on the Activity tab. 03 Complete the step on the page. The coach follows supported page and form changes and updates its next instruction. If the card asks you to review details, check them before selecting i have reviewed the details. Choose and save files using the application controls, then check its success message. 04 Ask for help or change direction. Select i can't see that control if the suggested control is missing. Select read in comprehensive manual for the full procedure. end walkthrough stops the active guide. Asking another question also ends it and answers your new question.

manual-topic-orientation-manage-the-coac.title: Manage the Coach Conversation
manual-topic-orientation-manage-the-coac.text: Stop answer cancels an answer that is still being prepared. New conversation starts a fresh conversation and ends the active walkthrough. Minimizing the panel only hides it; it does not cancel the answer. Conversation continuity is for the current signed-in browser tab, not a shared chat history across devices. New conversation does not delete the administrator's request log. Questions, responses, the requesting user, and basic page context are recorded for review. The coach does not collect the contents of page fields; information you type into the question is included. Do not put passwords or other secrets in a question.

manual-topic-orientation-rate-an-answer-.title: Rate an Answer and Report a Missing Control
manual-topic-orientation-rate-an-answer-.text: Use helpful when an answer helps you complete or understand the task, or needs work when it is incorrect, confusing, or irrelevant. You can change your rating; the latest selection is saved. During a walkthrough, i can't see that control records the missing-control problem with the current page and guided step. Feedback enters an administrator review queue together with failed or slow answers. It helps identify missing manual instructions, incorrect workflow steps, and service problems. A rating does not immediately rewrite the manual or train the model. Improvements are checked against the application and tested before reuse; you do not need to write a replacement answer yourself.

manual-topic-orientation-find-a-topic-in.title: Find a Topic in This Manual
manual-topic-orientation-find-a-topic-in.text: Use Search the manual at the top of this page, or press / to move to it. Results list specific topics with a short excerpt. Select a result, or press Enter for the first match, to jump to the highlighted text. Matching troubleshooting entries open automatically. Use Clear, or press Esc in the search field, to restore the full manual. The fixed bar at the bottom of the window has Top and Bottom links to jump to either end of the page. In the Comprehensive User Guide PDF, use your reader's Find command, bookmarks, and the guide's page navigation.

manual-topic-orientation-browse-longer-l.title: Browse Longer Lists
manual-topic-orientation-browse-longer-l.text: Use Records per page, where available, to choose 20, 50, or 100 records. Each list remembers your preferred size in this browser. Use the page numbers, Previous, or Next to move through results. Search and sorting apply to the full result list, so you do not need to search each page separately.

manual-topic-orientation-read-lists-and-.title: Read Lists and Tables
manual-topic-orientation-read-lists-and-.text: Table headings stay together where space permits, while long owner names can wrap within their column. On narrow screens, scroll wide tables horizontally or use the page's card layout to read the full record. When a row or card has a linked record name, you can select the surrounding row or card to open that record. Checkboxes, action buttons, and other links still perform their own actions. Keyboard users can tab to the record link and press Enter.

manual-topic-orientation-read-the-page-f.title: Read the Page Footer
manual-topic-orientation-read-the-page-f.text: The copyright line identifies the application version and, when available, its build date and source revision. Use that information when reporting a problem.

manual-topic-orientation-common-action-i.title: Common Action Icons
manual-topic-orientation-common-action-i.text: View - Open details Edit - Change a record Start - Begin a task Complete - Confirm and finish a task Archive - Hide reversibly Restore - Return to active Delete - Remove permanently Archive first. Archiving is reversible and keeps history. Permanent deletion is limited to administrators, requires freshly confirmed administrator access, and cannot be undone. In a task's related-record search or the Inbox engagement search, Enter runs the search without saving the task or filing the message. Choose the intended result, then use the explicit Save action. Enter on a focused button activates that button.

manual-topic-orientation-collapse-sideba.title: Collapse Sidebar Sections
manual-topic-orientation-collapse-sideba.text: Select a sidebar section heading to collapse or expand its links. The app remembers your choice. Expand Work to reach Reimbursements; administrators find Reimbursement Setup under Administration. If a link seems missing, check the collapsed headings and scroll the menu. The account controls remain at the bottom.

manual-topic-orientation-save-and-return.title: Save and Return with Confidence
manual-topic-orientation-save-and-return.text: Some forms keep a draft in this browser as you type. If you return before saving, use Restore Draft to bring it back or Discard Draft to start fresh. A browser draft is not a saved record, and selected files must be chosen again. On shared computers, discard drafts you no longer need. If someone changed the record while your form was open, compare a fresh view before saving again. Follow the message on screen; do not repeatedly submit an old form. Use the page's Back or Cancel link to return to the list or record you came from.

manual-topic-orientation-save-cancel-and.title: Save, cancel, and recover a draft
manual-topic-orientation-save-cancel-and.text: Required fields are marked in the forms. Correct the listed errors and save again if validation fails. Cancel returns without saving the current form. When you create a related organization or contact from an inquiry/contact form, MOED carries the draft back to the original form. Confirm the selected relationship after returning. If another person changes a record while you are editing, MOED may report a conflict. Preserve your unsaved text, reload the latest record, and reapply only the changes that still belong. A reload is also the first step after an expired request. Keyboard users can use the Skip to main content link, Tab/Shift+Tab, and the visible focus indication. Reduce-motion preferences suppress attention animations while retaining due-state color cues.

manual-topic-orientation-use-enter-witho.title: Use Enter without losing your place
manual-topic-orientation-use-enter-witho.text: In the related-record search on a task or the engagement search in the Inbox, Enter runs the search. It does not save the task or file the message. Review the results, choose the intended destination, then use the explicit Save action. Inquiry organization/contact searches and the engagement contact picker also use Enter to search. Use Tab to move between controls; Enter on a focused button activates that button. In the bulk-user deletion review, type DELETE USERS and press Enter or select Permanently delete. The Are you sure? dialog still requires confirmation. Cancel closes the dialog without deleting; Cancel on the review page abandons the selection. Financial Closeout offers Save draft before Finalize. Enter in an amount field saves a draft; use the explicit finalization control after reviewing the required completion conditions.

manual-topic-orientation-sidebar-and-val.title: Sidebar and Validation Updates
manual-topic-orientation-sidebar-and-val.text: Sidebar section headings expand/collapse and remember the user choice. Scroll the central menu independently of the logo/account area. On narrow screens, close the navigation drawer before continuing the form. AI Coach highlights and walkthrough spacing help locate controls; the coach still cannot click, save, or send on your behalf. Relationship selectors return bounded results. Refine the search if a desired organization/contact is not listed; selected existing values remain available. Validation summaries link directly to invalid fields. Correct required fields and save; do not discard the entire form solely because a result is outside the initial search page.

manual-topic-orientation-find-help-by-ta.title: Find help by task
manual-topic-orientation-find-help-by-ta.text: Figure 01. Find help by task. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Open User Manual from the sidebar. Browse the 14 chapters or choose a popular help topic. 02 Open View Comprehensive User Guide for the illustrated PDF. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Daily dashboard (p. 13) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-orientation-dark-theme.title: Dark theme
manual-topic-orientation-dark-theme.text: Figure 02. Dark theme. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Select Dark Theme in the sidebar to use the dark palette. 02 Select Light Theme to return. The preference is remembered by this browser. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Daily dashboard (p. 13) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-orientation-navigation-on-a.title: Navigation on a phone
manual-topic-orientation-navigation-on-a.text: Figure 03. Navigation on a phone. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Tap the menu button to open navigation. The close button, logo, and profile/sign-out block stay in place. 02 Scroll the menu between the fixed controls to reach other areas, including User Manual. 03 Choose an area, use Close navigation, tap outside the panel, or press Esc. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Daily dashboard (p. 13) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-orientation-recover-a-local.title: Recover a local browser draft
manual-topic-orientation-recover-a-local.text: Figure 04. Recover a local browser draft. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Use Save Draft to keep supported form text in this browser. 02 On return, choose Restore Draft to bring it back, or Discard Draft to clear it. 03 Review restored text against the current record; files and changes on another browser are not restored. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Daily dashboard (p. 13) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-roles-roles-and-access.title: Roles and Access
manual-topic-roles-roles-and-access.text: Everyone can read the shared operational picture. Editing and destructive actions are deliberately narrower. Related chapters: Profile and security (p. 124) / Administration (p. 138) / Reimbursements (p. 105) Capability Reviewer Editor Administrator View records, Chron, work, map, and exports Yes Yes Yes Manage own profile, calendar links, and security Yes Yes Yes Create and edit inquiries, engagements, organizations, contacts, and speakers No Yes Yes Manage tasks, Chron entries, closeouts, and engagement email No Yes Yes Add, edit, archive, and restore email templates No Yes Yes Archive and restore shared records No Yes Yes Manage users, network diagnostics, audit history, backups, and permanent deletion No No Yes

manual-topic-roles-read-and-export.title: Read and Export
manual-topic-roles-read-and-export.text: Reviewers can inspect shared records, follow links between them, use search and filters, copy presentation briefs, view presentation and QR-code PDFs, review link statistics, and subscribe to the calendar.

manual-topic-roles-coordinate-and-mainta.title: Coordinate and Maintain
manual-topic-roles-coordinate-and-mainta.text: Editors add reviewer capabilities plus record creation, editing, archive/restore, task management, Chron maintenance, financial closeout, engagement email, and inbound email review.

manual-topic-roles-govern-and-recover.title: Govern and Recover
manual-topic-roles-govern-and-recover.text: Administrators add user profile and lifecycle controls, remote network diagnostics, audit inspection, encrypted backups, permanent deletion, and access to deployment signals. Sensitive actions require fresh password and 2FA confirmation.

manual-topic-roles-preview-role-permissi.title: Preview role permissions
manual-topic-roles-preview-role-permissi.text: Figure 05. Preview role permissions. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Administrators can expand Preview access in the sidebar and select Editor or Reviewer. 02 Apply changes the menus and effective permissions. Return to Administrator ends the preview. 03 Preview actions affect application data. Use a separate sample environment when practicing. Related chapters: Profile and security (p. 124) / Administration (p. 138) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-dashboard-daily-dashboard.title: Daily Dashboard
manual-topic-dashboard-daily-dashboard.text: The Dashboard answers three questions: what is coming, what is yours, and what is incomplete. Related chapters: Booking pipeline (p. 16) / Engagements (p. 26) / Work queue (p. 77) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-dashboard-daily-summary.title: Daily Summary
manual-topic-dashboard-daily-summary.text: The compact top cards distinguish all active work from your own active and overdue work. The Dashboard loads its workload and readiness summaries efficiently as records grow. Shared counts link to the booking pipeline, financial closeouts, and - when available to your role - inbound mail awaiting review. Purple marks Mail For Review and the mail-review alert. The

manual-topic-dashboard-financial-closeou.title: Financial Closeouts
manual-topic-dashboard-financial-closeou.text: panel uses gold to distinguish unfinished financial reports.

manual-topic-dashboard-primary-panels.title: Primary Panels
manual-topic-dashboard-primary-panels.text: My Work leads with assigned tasks by urgency and due date, alongside Upcoming Engagements. Open the Booking pipeline disclosure below Needs Attention for inquiry next actions and pipeline health. My Work and Inquiry Next Actions show a short due date with a second line such as 1 day overdue, Due today, Due tomorrow, or Upcoming for later dates. Items more than 3 days overdue pulse red in a repeating cascade to draw your attention. For inquiries, this is based on the next-action due date.

manual-topic-dashboard-event-readiness.title: Event Readiness
manual-topic-dashboard-event-readiness.text: Readiness flags an unconfirmed event, missing venue address, missing presentation, or missing event contact assignment. Open the event to complete the missing details. Financial Closeouts Ended events remain here until actual giving, lodging, travel, and book-table receipts are finalized. The age indicator shows how many days the report has been waiting.

manual-topic-dashboard-follow-dashboard-.title: Follow Dashboard Date Windows
manual-topic-dashboard-follow-dashboard-.text: Dashboard links to inquiries and upcoming engagements carry the relevant view or date window into the destination list. Review the destination filters before interpreting its counts. On Engagements, change the start/end date filters or clear them to see a broader period.

manual-topic-dashboard-read-task-timing-.title: Read Task Timing and Financial Follow-Up
manual-topic-dashboard-read-task-timing-.text: In My Tasks, use the due date and urgency label to decide what needs attention first. The timing bar gives context for the deadline; open the task for the full details. In Financial Closeouts, since event tells you how long ago the event ended. It is different from a task's due date. Open the event's closeout to review what remains.

manual-topic-dashboard-dashboard-work-an.title: Dashboard work and task timing
manual-topic-dashboard-dashboard-work-an.text: Figure 06. Dashboard work and task timing. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Use the task counts and My Tasks rows to choose work. 02 Deadline bars show timing and urgency alongside the written due date; open a task for its details. Related chapters: Booking pipeline (p. 16) / Engagements (p. 26) / Work queue (p. 77) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-dashboard-financial-follow-.title: Financial follow-up since the event
manual-topic-dashboard-financial-follow-.text: Figure 07. Financial follow-up since the event. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Review Needs Attention and Financial Closeouts. 02 Read the elapsed time since the event alongside its dates, then open the event to finish its report. Related chapters: Booking pipeline (p. 16) / Engagements (p. 26) / Work queue (p. 77) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-booking-pipeline-inquiry-an.title: Inquiry and Booking Pipeline
manual-topic-booking-pipeline-inquiry-an.text: Use an Inquiry for a possible event that is not booked yet. It keeps early communication and follow-up visible without creating a partly known Engagement. Related chapters: Engagements (p. 26) / Work queue (p. 77) / Chron and email (p. 89)

manual-topic-booking-pipeline-inquiry-fi.title: Inquiry First, Engagement After Booking
manual-topic-booking-pipeline-inquiry-fi.text: The Inquiry is the source record for qualification. Converting it creates the Engagement once an organization, title, and preferred date range are known. The original Inquiry then becomes read-only and remains linked for reference.

manual-topic-booking-pipeline-work-the-p.title: Work the Pipeline
manual-topic-booking-pipeline-work-the-p.text: 01 Capture the request. Select New Inquiry in the Booking Pipeline. Add the organization and contact when known; they can remain blank during early triage. 02 Assign the next action. Choose an owner and priority, then state the concrete next step and its due date. The pipeline cards and Dashboard emphasize this action. 03 Move the stage. Use New > Contacted > Qualified > Awaiting Details > Proposal Sent as the normal path. Move backward when the facts warrant it. Declining requires a reason and can be reopened later. 04 Keep the history together. Open the Inquiry and use the Activity, Correspondence, and Tasks tabs to keep decisions, email, and follow-up work together. Open a message from Correspondence to review delivery or retry a failed delivery while the Inquiry is active. 05 Review the booking. Select Convert to Engagement when the request is ready. Check the imported engagement details, availability warnings, and which open tasks should move. Clearing every task checkbox moves none. If a next action remains, explicitly carry it forward as a task or resolve it with a reason; the original action and your decision remain in history. Warnings require acknowledgement but remain a deliberate, auditable decision. 06 Continue in the Engagement. Conversion creates the Engagement, assigns the Inquiry's primary contact as Primary Host when available, moves selected work, and adds the standard event checklist. Replies to earlier Inquiry correspondence continue into the converted Engagement.

manual-topic-booking-pipeline-filter-the.title: Filter the Board
manual-topic-booking-pipeline-filter-the.text: Search request text, organizations, contacts, and locations. Use the owner and next-action filters to find your inquiries, unassigned work, overdue actions, or requests that still need a next step.

manual-topic-booking-pipeline-use-the-st.title: Use the Starting Templates
manual-topic-booking-pipeline-use-the-st.text: Initial response, request details, date options, and proposal follow-up templates are editable before sending. Sent messages appear in Correspondence and Chron with delivery status.

manual-topic-booking-pipeline-keep-the-s.title: Keep the Source Record
manual-topic-booking-pipeline-keep-the-s.text: Do not copy pre-booking Chron Log Entries by hand. The booked Inquiry retains its source email, stage history, Chron, correspondence, and any work not moved to the Engagement. Resolve or reassign active Inquiries before archiving their Contact or Organization. The default board shows active inquiries and those booked this month. Use the Stage filter for Booked, Declined, or All Stages. In All Stages, Declined starts on a separate row. The stages wrap to fit your screen; scroll down to see the remaining rows.

manual-topic-booking-pipeline-archive-fi.title: Archive Finished Inquiries
manual-topic-booking-pipeline-archive-fi.text: After declining an Inquiry or converting a booked Inquiry to an Engagement, administrators and editors can select Archive Inquiry on its card or detail page. It leaves the Booking Pipeline and its Dashboard count while all details, history, correspondence, tasks, and the Engagement link remain available. Open Archived Inquiries from the Booking Pipeline to search, filter, export, or review retained records. Select Restore Inquiry to return one to its previous outcome. Restore a declined Inquiry before editing or reopening it. Its Engagement and follow-up tasks keep their existing state.

manual-topic-booking-pipeline-archive-a-.title: Archive a finished inquiry
manual-topic-booking-pipeline-archive-a-.text: Open a declined inquiry or an inquiry that was booked and converted to an engagement. Select Archive Inquiry in the Archive This Inquiry panel or on its pipeline card. Archiving retains the stage, request details, activity, correspondence, tasks, and any surviving engagement link. It removes the inquiry from ordinary pipeline views, counts, and exports, and hides its tasks from active work until restored. It does not archive or change the engagement. Choose Archived Inquiries to search retained records or export that view. Open an archived inquiry to read its information, or select Restore Inquiry to return it to its original Booked or Declined stage. Restore a declined inquiry before reopening it to Qualified. A booked inquiry remains a read-only source record after restoration. A recorded conversion still permits archiving when its engagement was later deleted; an inquiry merely labeled Booked without a recorded conversion is not eligible.

manual-topic-booking-pipeline-read-and-f.title: Read and filter the booking board
manual-topic-booking-pipeline-read-and-f.text: Figure 08. Read and filter the booking board. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Search requests and narrow by owner, stage, or next action. 02 Open a card to review the request and its next step. The default view includes active inquiries and bookings from this month. 03 Archive Inquiry is available for declined requests and recorded bookings. Archived Inquiries opens retained records outside the current pipeline. Related chapters: Engagements (p. 26) / Work queue (p. 77) / Chron and email (p. 89)

manual-topic-booking-pipeline-review-an-.title: Review an inquiry
manual-topic-booking-pipeline-review-an-.text: Figure 09. Review an inquiry. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Review the preferred and alternate dates, priority, owner, and next action. 02 Use Activity, Correspondence, and Tasks to switch the working panel. 03 Change stage as the request develops; a decline needs a reason and can be reopened. Related chapters: Engagements (p. 26) / Work queue (p. 77) / Chron and email (p. 89)

manual-topic-booking-pipeline-capture-th.title: Capture the request and date options
manual-topic-booking-pipeline-capture-th.text: Figure 10. Capture the request and date options. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Enter the request title and summary. Choose the organization and primary contact when known. 02 Record preferred dates, alternate dates, event type, and location. 03 Choose an owner, priority, source, next action, and due date, then save. Related chapters: Engagements (p. 26) / Work queue (p. 77) / Chron and email (p. 89)

manual-topic-booking-pipeline-give-the-i.title: Give the inquiry a next action
manual-topic-booking-pipeline-give-the-i.text: Figure 11. Give the inquiry a next action. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Keep the next action concrete, such as sending date options or requesting room details. 02 Set a due date so the pipeline and Dashboard can highlight it. 03 Use Source Detail for a referral, mailbox, form, or campaign reference. Related chapters: Engagements (p. 26) / Work queue (p. 77) / Chron and email (p. 89)

manual-topic-booking-pipeline-convert-a-.title: Convert a qualified inquiry
manual-topic-booking-pipeline-convert-a-.text: Figure 12. Convert a qualified inquiry. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Review the proposed engagement and any schedule conflicts. 02 Choose the open inquiry tasks to move; clearing every box moves none. 03 Carry an unresolved next action forward as a task, or resolve it with a reason. 04 Acknowledge any availability warnings before confirming the conversion. Related chapters: Engagements (p. 26) / Work queue (p. 77) / Chron and email (p. 89)

manual-topic-booking-pipeline-write-inqu.title: Write inquiry correspondence
manual-topic-booking-pipeline-write-inqu.text: Figure 13. Write inquiry correspondence. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Choose Initial response, Request details, Date options, or Proposal follow-up. 02 Verify the primary contact, then edit the subject and plain-text message. 03 Queue the message when ready; its signed inquiry marker keeps replies connected. Screenshot context: The screenshot preview has mail delivery disabled. The form is shown without sending a message. Related chapters: Engagements (p. 26) / Work queue (p. 77) / Chron and email (p. 89)

manual-topic-booking-pipeline-archive-a-.title: Archive a booked or declined inquiry
manual-topic-booking-pipeline-archive-a-.text: Figure 14. Archive a booked or declined inquiry. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Finish declining the request or booking and converting it to an engagement. Open the inquiry. 02 Select Archive Inquiry. Its details, history, correspondence, tasks, and engagement link are retained. 03 The inquiry leaves ordinary pipeline views. Archiving this source inquiry does not archive its engagement. Related chapters: Engagements (p. 26) / Work queue (p. 77) / Chron and email (p. 89)

manual-topic-booking-pipeline-find-and-r.title: Find and restore archived inquiries
manual-topic-booking-pipeline-find-and-r.text: Figure 15. Find and restore archived inquiries. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Choose Archived Inquiries from the pipeline or the archive panel on an inquiry. 02 Search retained Booked and Declined records. Export downloads the filtered archived view. 03 Open a title to read its retained information. Restore Inquiry returns it to its original stage; restore a declined inquiry before reopening it. Related chapters: Engagements (p. 26) / Work queue (p. 77) / Chron and email (p. 89)

manual-topic-engagements-engagements.title: Engagements
manual-topic-engagements-engagements.text: An engagement is the operational record for one event: the schedule, assigned people, presentations, logistics, planning state, communication history, work, and final receipts. Related chapters: People and organizations (p. 61) / Work queue (p. 77) / Chron and email (p. 89) / Map and calendar (p. 96)

manual-topic-engagements-search-broadly.title: Search Broadly
manual-topic-engagements-search-broadly.text: The Engagements search checks event titles and descriptions, organizations, contacts, caller names, active Chron text, and Chron authors. Unquoted words are alternatives; words inside one quoted group must all match. Terms shorter than three characters are ignored. Example: conference "travel confirmed"

manual-topic-engagements-filter-precisel.title: Filter Precisely
manual-topic-engagements-filter-precisel.text: Switch between current and archived records, filter by lifecycle, then sort by organization, date, confirmation, or lifecycle. The summary cards show current lifecycle totals. The table shows event dates, lifecycle, confirmation, and whether financial closeout is open, closed, or not applicable. Select the title or View icon for the full record.

manual-topic-engagements-create-or-edit-.title: Create or Edit an Engagement
manual-topic-engagements-create-or-edit-.text: 01 Open the form, then choose Organization. Editors and administrators: open Engagements and select + New Engagement. Choose the active Organization inside the New Engagement form; Organization Details does not provide a new-event action. If needed, create the organization first, then return to this form. To change an existing event, open its details and select Edit Engagement instead. 02 Name and schedule the event. Enter a required event title, an optional description, a valid start and end date, and an event type. Use Other when the preset types do not fit. 03 Assign event contacts. Select multiple existing contacts and give each any applicable event roles: Primary host, On-site contact, Billing, Travel, or Materials. Search the directory to add another person, or use Add new contact repeatedly. New contacts and organization affiliations are saved with the event. 04 Add presentations. Choose a saved speaker from the dropdown; add missing speakers in Relationships > Speakers. Presentation details can be filled in later. Dates must fall within the event range, and duration is entered in minutes. Record actual attendance afterward, including zero when applicable. At least one complete presentation is required before the engagement can be Confirmed. 05 Capture logistics. Record book-table and brochure permissions, travel coverage, planned compensation, travel/lodging estimates, lodging type, and the physical event location. 06 Set planning states and ownership. Choose lifecycle and confirmation, then select the Caller when that person should own the initial standard checklist. If no Caller is selected, the checklist belongs to the user creating the engagement. Add an initial Chron entry when there is context worth preserving. On Edit Engagement, Save Changes and Cancel stay visible in the bar at the bottom of the window as you scroll. Save Changes saves the entire engagement form, including presentation details and pending file changes.

manual-topic-engagements-lifecycle.title: Lifecycle
manual-topic-engagements-lifecycle.text: Active The event is moving forward. Postponed The original is paused and may link to its replacement. Canceled A reason is required; open event tasks are canceled automatically. Completed The event has finished. Finalizing its financial report also sets this state.

manual-topic-engagements-confirmation.title: Confirmation
manual-topic-engagements-confirmation.text: Work in Progress Details are still being assembled. Under Review The plan is ready for checking or decision. Confirmed The commitment is agreed and at least one complete presentation exists. Lifecycle and confirmation are independent. A postponed event can retain its former confirmation state, while a completed event may reflect the confirmation state it reached during planning. The Engagements list starts with All lifecycle states. Your selection is remembered for your account in this browser. Use Lifecycle to narrow the list to Active, Postponed, Canceled, or Completed; the separate Current/Archived view controls whether archived records appear.

manual-topic-engagements-presentation-fi.title: Presentation Files, QR Codes, and History
manual-topic-engagements-presentation-fi.text: Files belong to an individual presentation. From an event's detail page, select the Presentations tab, then Edit Presentations. Find the intended presentation and its speaker before choosing a file. A PowerPoint is not attached directly to an organization or to the engagement as a whole.

manual-topic-engagements-pdf-speaker-not.title: PDF Speaker Notes
manual-topic-engagements-pdf-speaker-not.text: Attach one PDF up to 100 MB to each presentation with Choose PDF, or drag one file onto Drop PDF here. Select Save Changes to upload it. Select View PDF Speaker Notes on the event detail page to open it in a new tab. Use Replace PDF or Remove current PDF on the edit page and save to update it. Use this file for notes you intend to share: anyone with its QR code can open the PDF without signing in.

manual-topic-engagements-ppt-slidedeck.title: PPT Slidedeck
manual-topic-engagements-ppt-slidedeck.text: Attach one PowerPoint .ppt or .pptx file up to 500 MB with Choose PPT, or drag one file onto Drop PowerPoint here. Select Save Changes to upload it. Use Replace PPT or Remove current PPT and save to update it. Download PPT Slidedeck, next to the notes button, downloads the file to open in PowerPoint. When editing an engagement, Save Changes uploads PowerPoint and PDF files in small pieces, with a progress indicator. Keep the page open until saving finishes. Interrupted transfers retry automatically; if an error remains, select Save Changes to retry. PowerPoint files may be up to 500 MB; PDFs may be up to 100 MB. Anyone with the PPT Slidedeck QR link can download the file without signing in. Replacing it keeps the same QR code and statistics. Removing it hides the code and stops downloads; uploading again restores the same link.

manual-topic-engagements-speaker-qr-code.title: Speaker QR Codes
manual-topic-engagements-speaker-qr-code.text: Saving creates separate codes for each presentation's available speaker resources: website, bio, donations, connection, blog, books, custom links, notes, and PPT Slidedeck. Select a displayed code to copy its image. Select the Copy Link icon beneath a code's image to copy its web address for an email, message, or document. These controls appear when viewing or editing a presentation. Download PNG or SVG images when you prefer to save a file for your slides or handouts. File codes appear after you upload and save the corresponding PDF or PowerPoint. Replacing a file keeps its existing QR code and link, so shared slides and handouts continue to work. Removing a file hides its code; uploading it again reuses the link and its statistics. Select View QR Codes PDF, choose the codes to include, then select Prepare PDF to view, save, or print a single landscape sheet with those labeled codes, schedule, and venue. Use Select all to include every available code. Drag any code by its handle to reorder the list, whether checked or unchecked. Only checked codes appear in the PDF, in that order from left to right and then top to bottom. Keyboard users can focus a handle and press the Up or Down arrow key. Missing schedule details show To be confirmed. Disabled codes are labeled; file codes without an uploaded PDF or PowerPoint and previous speakers' codes are left out. Viewing the sheet does not add visits. Use Edit Presentations on the event's Presentations tab to open the presentation section of Edit Engagement. Numbered headings such as Presentation 1 and Presentation 2 separate the entries; check the topic and speaker before changing a file. File replacement and removal remain pending until you select Save Changes in the persistent bottom bar; the notice beside the PDF or PPT identifies the pending change. Choose replacement or removal, not both, then save and check the updated file details. Presentations can be archived and restored separately from the event. When restoring, update any date that falls outside the event's current date range. Administrators can permanently delete presentations after confirming their access; their scoped statistics reset actions appear with the saved presentation's management controls. When postponing or canceling an event, link it to a replacement from the same organization. MOED displays both "rescheduled as" and "rescheduled from" references and prevents circular links.

manual-topic-engagements-manage-email-te.title: Manage Email Templates
manual-topic-engagements-manage-email-te.text: Open Email Templates under Work in the sidebar, or select Manage Email Templates in the engagement email composer. This library supplies engagement email in the browser and Mattermost. Inquiry emails use their own starting templates. 01 Add or edit a template. Select + New Email Template, or open an active template by its name or Edit action. Enter the template name, subject, and plain-text message. The original Booking confirmation, Travel and lodging request, Final-detail reconfirmation, Presentation schedule, and Post-event thank-you templates can all be edited. 02 Personalize the starting text. Expand Personalize with event fields. Click where the field belongs in the subject or message, then choose a field button. Event name, organization, dates, location, and speaker names are available; Presentation schedule belongs in the message only. For example, Welcome to {{event_name}} uses that engagement's event name when composing. The routing marker is added automatically. 03 Choose suggestions and order. Select the event contact roles to suggest when this template is chosen. Leave them clear to choose contacts when composing. Lower Display order numbers appear first. Speakers are always a separate sender choice; inserting Speaker names into the message does not add recipients. 04 Save and review. Select Create Template or Save Changes. Choose the saved template in an engagement email to review the filled subject, message, and recipients before queuing. When you entered the library from an engagement, Return to Email takes you back to its composer.

manual-topic-engagements-archive-and-res.title: Archive and Restore
manual-topic-engagements-archive-and-res.text: Search the library by name or subject. Archive removes a template from new emails in both composers. Open Archived to view it or select Restore to make it available again. Restore an archived template before editing it.

manual-topic-engagements-delete-and-acce.title: Delete and Access
manual-topic-engagements-delete-and-acce.text: Editors and administrators can add, edit, archive, and restore templates. Reviewers can view them. Only administrators can permanently Delete an archived template, after confirming their access. Deletion cannot be undone; sent messages, their template names, and Chron history remain available. Changes apply to future messages. A draft already open in a composer keeps its reviewed text. If its template is archived or deleted before sending, review the preserved draft as Custom message or choose another template. If another session changed a template while you were editing, keep a copy of your draft, reload, and review the latest version before saving. Custom message is always available, even when every saved template is archived.

manual-topic-engagements-review-qr-code-.title: Review QR Code Activity
manual-topic-engagements-review-qr-code-.text: • In the Presentations tab, select Statistics beneath a code to see its visits. Open a speaker's record and choose Statistics for activity across that speaker's presentations. • Choose a date range to focus on a recent event or a longer period. In the speaker view, use Link Type to focus on notes, donations, or Custom Links, then select Apply Filters. • Use the charts to see when and where links were opened. Hover or tap for details, or expand the data tables for exact counts. These are visits to links, not an attendance count. Opening a shared QR link records a visit. Use Copy Link to share that same link; copying an image or link does not itself add a visit. To change where an existing code leads, editors and administrators can open that code's Statistics, edit Destination, and select Save Link. The printed code continues to work. Clear Link enabled and save to stop access through that code. For Speaker Notes or PPT Slidedeck, replace the file on the presentation instead of editing a destination. Select Combined Presentation Statistics in the upper-right of a presentation's pane to see total visits, activity over time, and combined referrer, browser, country, and operating system breakdowns. Date filters use the configured local time zone, and Clear Filters keeps the report scoped to that presentation. Disabled codes and previous speakers' codes retain their historical visits. A person opening multiple codes contributes multiple visits. Use Statistics on an individual code for its own report, or Back to Presentation to return to the presentation. Editing a speaker's profile does not change destinations already shared with audiences. Previous speakers' links and uploaded files remain separate when you change a presentation's speaker.

manual-topic-engagements-send-and-track-.title: Send and Track Event Email
manual-topic-engagements-send-and-track-.text: Editors and administrators can send email from an active engagement. Use Send Email near the page heading or Send Message in the Correspondence section. Every message remains easy to find there afterward. 01 Choose a starting template. Choose an active template from the shared library, or Custom message to write from scratch. Event fields are filled from this engagement. Template text is only a starting point; edit the subject and body before sending. Use Manage Email Templates to learn how to maintain the library. 02 Select recipients. Use the Primary host, On-site contact, Billing, Travel, Materials, or Speaker shortcuts, or select individual recipient cards. Speakers assigned to active presentations are optional and unchecked by default. Choose the Speaker shortcut or check a speaker card to include them. You may send to speakers alone. Changing templates keeps your speaker selection. Choose To, Cc, or Bcc in each selected card. To and Cc addresses are visible to everyone receiving the email; Bcc addresses stay hidden. Under Send yourself a copy, choose Cc Me or Bcc Me to include your account email. Only valid email addresses can receive a message. Matching addresses receive one copy; use the same recipient type for a shared address. 03 Review the routing marker. The exact engagement marker is included in every template subject and is added automatically if removed. When inbound mail is enabled, replies return through the shared mailbox and the marker helps place them in the right engagement Chron. 04 Optionally append the event brief. The share-safe brief includes the public event schedule, venue, description, and presentations. It deliberately excludes Chron, internal notes, compensation, giving, and financial-closeout information. Preview it before queuing. 05 Send and check the result. Select Queue Email, then use the Correspondence list to see whether each recipient is waiting, sent, or failed. If a recipient remains failed, open the message and select Retry Failed Deliveries. If it says Delivery Uncertain, check with your mail provider or recipient before selecting Retry Reviewed Deliveries; the message may already have arrived.

manual-topic-engagements-one-place-to-ch.title: One Place to Check
manual-topic-engagements-one-place-to-ch.text: Open the outbound message to review what was sent, who it was sent to, and the result for each address.

manual-topic-engagements-automatic-chron.title: Automatic Chron History
manual-topic-engagements-automatic-chron.text: The message is added to the Engagement, Organization, and selected Contact Chron logs. Select View Outbound Message from a Chron entry to return to its delivery record.

manual-topic-engagements-view-share-and-.title: View, Share, and Close the Event
manual-topic-engagements-view-share-and-.text: The event detail page shows its unique email routing marker. The built-in outbound composer inserts it automatically. When using another mail application, select the copy icon immediately beside the marker and keep it in the email subject or plain-text body when that message should route to the engagement's Chron log. In the Presentations tab, open Export Presentation at the bottom of a presentation card. Briefs include that presentation's speaker, schedule, duration, and attendance, with its event and venue context.

manual-topic-engagements-copy-text.title: Copy Text
manual-topic-engagements-copy-text.text: Copies a plain-text presentation brief for messages or notes.

manual-topic-engagements-copy-md.title: Copy MD
manual-topic-engagements-copy-md.text: Copies a Markdown-formatted presentation brief for systems that support structured text.

manual-topic-engagements-view-pdf.title: View PDF
manual-topic-engagements-view-pdf.text: Opens a branded brief for the selected presentation in your browser for viewing, saving, or printing.

manual-topic-engagements-view-qr-codes-p.title: View QR Codes PDF
manual-topic-engagements-view-qr-codes-p.text: Lets you choose which of that presentation's QR codes to include, then opens a themed landscape sheet. Editors and administrators can use Financial Closeout to save a receipt draft while work is still pending. Enter Giving Received, Lodging Received, Travel Received, and Book Table Received before finalizing. Leave unknown amounts blank while saving a draft; enter zero only when nothing was received. Drafts are excluded from finalized financial history. The original planning estimates remain unchanged. Every event task due on or before the last active presentation must first be marked Completed; canceled tasks still block until truthfully resolved, while later and undated tasks do not hold closeout. Confirm that the amounts are final to complete the engagement; later corrections retain the original close date and record the update.

manual-topic-engagements-archive-and-del.title: Archive and Delete Carefully
manual-topic-engagements-archive-and-del.text: Archive removes the engagement from current views but keeps its history available for restoration. When deletion is permitted, it removes the event and its event-specific presentations, Chron, tasks, and contact role assignments. Finalized financial history prevents permanent deletion; archive that event to retain its history. Prefer archive unless removal is explicitly required.

manual-topic-engagements-inspect-tracked.title: Inspect Tracked Visit Details
manual-topic-engagements-inspect-tracked.text: Presentation QR/resource cards show tracked visit totals. Open the event statistics and filter by Speaker, Link Type, From, and Through. Expand the detailed visits, group dates as offered, and select chart points or table rows to inspect the matching activity. Dates use the configured local time zone shown by the controls. A tracked visit is not proof that a person read a document; downloading a resource through its tracked link and directly opening an untracked file URL are different paths.

manual-topic-engagements-archive-or-dele.title: Archive or Delete a Presentation
manual-topic-engagements-archive-or-dele.text: 01 Open the right presentation. Open the engagement, select Presentations, then Edit Presentations. Find the numbered presentation block and check its topic and speaker. 02 Choose the action at the bottom of that block. Archive hides a saved presentation while keeping it available to restore. Editors and administrators can archive. Delete permanently removes that saved presentation and its associated resources and visit history; only administrators can delete. You can delete an active presentation directly; archiving first is not required. 03 Review and confirm. For Delete, unlock administrator actions if prompted, then select Delete again and read the confirmation. Select Delete Permanently only after checking the presentation, or choose Archive Instead to keep a restorable record. Cancel leaves it in place. Archive and Delete are separate actions: they do not save other unsaved edits on the page. To undo an archive, use Restore Archived Presentations for this engagement. Check that the restored presentation's date fits the event's current dates. Permanent deletion cannot be undone. Removing the last active presentation from a confirmed active engagement returns its confirmation to Under Review. Remove on a newly added, unsaved presentation only removes that draft block. The file-removal checkboxes remove a PDF or PowerPoint when you save; they do not delete the presentation.

manual-topic-engagements-review-planning.title: Review Planning and Retained History
manual-topic-engagements-review-planning.text: The engagement overview groups Next Action, Workflow, and Readiness so you can see the next step, event state, and missing essentials together. Use the tabs for Activity, Correspondence, Tasks, Presentations, Contacts, Logistics, and Financials. Edit Engagement groups related fields into cards; save with the persistent Save Changes bar. Event contacts can retain the name and role they had when assigned even if their organization affiliation later changes. Historical contact details explain earlier work; they are not automatically offered as current email recipients. Final financial reports retain correction history. Enter a reason when correcting one; archive events and organizations whose finalized financial history prevents permanent deletion.

manual-topic-engagements-reset-one-qr-li.title: Reset One QR Link or All Presentation Statistics
manual-topic-engagements-reset-one-qr-li.text: Administrators can use Reset Link Statistics beside a saved presentation's individual QR link to clear only that link's visits. Reset All Presentation Statistics at the bottom of the presentation block clears visits for all its links. Unlock administrator actions, check the named link or presentation on the review screen, and confirm the intended scope. Resetting visits keeps the presentation, files, and QR codes; cleared visit history cannot be recovered.

manual-topic-engagements-presentation-re.title: Presentation reference and file history
manual-topic-engagements-presentation-re.text: Presentations record topic, date, time, speaker, duration, and expected attendance. Their dates must fit the engagement before it can be confirmed. PDF Speaker Notes and PPT Slidedeck each show the current filename, size, upload time, and uploader where available. Each presentation can hold one PDF and one .ppt or .pptx file. Older files may have no recorded uploader. Selecting a replacement PDF or PowerPoint, or checking Remove, is pending until you select Save Changes in the persistent bar at the bottom of the Edit Engagement window. This saves the entire engagement form. The notice beside the file identifies the pending change. Choose replacement or removal, not both. Cancel or leave without saving to keep the current file; after saving, check the updated filename and upload details. Speaker Notes QR links open the PDF; PPT Slidedeck QR links download the PowerPoint. Both work without signing in. Copy link shares the encoded QR address, so visits follow the same link and appear in its statistics. Merely copying a link or image adds no visit. Direct file URLs and internal QR sheets do not add visits. Changing the speaker changes a presentation's current resources; previous-speaker codes remain in historical statistics. Archive or restore presentations separately from their engagement.

manual-topic-engagements-readiness-close.title: Readiness, closeout, and lifecycle effects
manual-topic-engagements-readiness-close.text: Use readiness to find missing presentations, contact details, or planning information. Correct the source record and revisit the panel. Canceling an event requires a reason and cancels its open tasks. Canceled tasks still block a closeout prerequisite that requires Completed. Changing event dates reschedules active generated tasks unless their dates were manually overridden. Postponed/canceled events can link to replacements at the same organization; circular links are rejected.

manual-topic-engagements-reset-presentat.title: Reset presentation statistics
manual-topic-engagements-reset-presentat.text: After fresh administrator confirmation, choose Reset All Presentation Statistics at the bottom of the presentation block, then Reset Statistics to Zero. This permanently removes all of its recorded link visits, including disabled and previous-speaker links. QR codes, destinations, uploaded PDFs and PowerPoints, and presentation details remain intact. Other presentations are unaffected; future visits start from zero.

manual-topic-engagements-restore-archive.title: Restore archived presentations
manual-topic-engagements-restore-archive.text: In the engagement editor, choose Restore Archived Presentations, select presentations, adjust dates/times to fit the active event, and choose Restore Selected. Each selected speaker must be valid. Administrators can permanently delete an archived presentation from this view after fresh confirmation.

manual-topic-engagements-engagement-filt.title: Engagement Filters and Visit Reporting
manual-topic-engagements-engagement-filt.text: Engagements provides start/end date filtering in addition to existing search/status controls. Links from dashboard upcoming-event and inquiry panes retain the relevant destination view. Clear or broaden filters before concluding a record is absent. Short-link statistics offers Speaker, Link Type, From and Through dates in the configured local time zone, Apply Filters, totals, and Referrers/Browsers/Countries/Operating Systems charts. Detailed visit rows identify event/resource context and use date grouping and chart highlighting where available. Presentation resource/QR cards show their tracked totals. Reset Statistics retains its separate administrator confirmation; viewing or filtering is read-only. Network > Remote Document Responses adds response/timing measurements for PDF and PowerPoint traffic. These operational counts are not equivalent to tracked public-link visits. Direct downloads and tracked link opens have different analytics paths.

manual-topic-engagements-financial-close.title: Financial Closeout: Four Required Receipt Categories
manual-topic-engagements-financial-close.text: Before finalizing an event, enter Giving Received, Lodging Received, Travel Received, and Book Table Received. Leave unknown amounts blank when saving a draft; enter 0 only after confirming no amount was received. The completion indicator counts all four categories, and the total includes book-table receipts. Book-table amounts remain separate from giving in organization totals and appear in final reports and correction history. Older finalized reports have no recorded book-table amount; MOED shows Not recorded rather than inventing zero. When correcting a report, enter every receipt category and explain the correction. Earlier revisions retain their original amounts.

manual-topic-engagements-find-an-engagem.title: Find an engagement
manual-topic-engagements-find-an-engagem.text: Figure 16. Find an engagement. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Start with All lifecycle states, or select Active, Postponed, Canceled, or Completed. Your choice is remembered for your account in this browser. 02 Current and Archived are separate from Lifecycle. Clear both filters when looking for a missing record. 03 Sort by organization, date, confirmation, or lifecycle. Open the event title or View action to continue planning. Related chapters: People and organizations (p. 61) / Work queue (p. 77) / Chron and email (p. 89) / Map and calendar (p. 96)

manual-topic-engagements-planning-overvi.title: Planning overview and record tabs
manual-topic-engagements-planning-overvi.text: Figure 17. Planning overview and record tabs. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Review Workflow, Readiness, and Next Action together. 02 Choose the relevant tab for activity, correspondence, tasks, presentations, contacts, logistics, or financials. Related chapters: People and organizations (p. 61) / Work queue (p. 77) / Chron and email (p. 89) / Map and calendar (p. 96)

manual-topic-engagements-edit-an-engagem.title: Edit an engagement in focused cards
manual-topic-engagements-edit-an-engagem.text: Figure 18. Edit an engagement in focused cards. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Work through Event Details & Schedule and the related cards. 02 Keep unsaved changes in this browser with Save Draft where offered, or save the record using Save Changes. Related chapters: People and organizations (p. 61) / Work queue (p. 77) / Chron and email (p. 89) / Map and calendar (p. 96)

manual-topic-engagements-read-retained-e.title: Read retained event contact assignments
manual-topic-engagements-read-retained-e.text: Figure 19. Read retained event contact assignments. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Open Contacts on the engagement. 02 Historical assignment identifies a contact whose event role is retained after their organization affiliation changes. 03 Use current affiliations when choosing recipients or assigning new roles. Related chapters: People and organizations (p. 61) / Work queue (p. 77) / Chron and email (p. 89) / Map and calendar (p. 96)

manual-topic-engagements-presentation-de.title: Presentation details and audience resources
manual-topic-engagements-presentation-de.text: Figure 20. Presentation details and audience resources. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Open Presentations and review the speaker, title, schedule, duration, and attendance. Use Edit Presentations to open the editing section. 02 Select View PDF Speaker Notes to open the notes, or Download PPT Slidedeck to save the PowerPoint for a compatible presentation app. 03 Select Copy link beneath a QR image to share its web address. Select the image to copy the QR graphic, or PNG/SVG to save it. 04 Combined Presentation Statistics covers all codes; Statistics beneath a code opens its own activity. Screenshot context: The first row of resource codes is shown. Scroll down to find the file and custom-resource codes. Related chapters: People and organizations (p. 61) / Work queue (p. 77) / Chron and email (p. 89) / Map and calendar (p. 96)

manual-topic-engagements-share-a-powerpo.title: Share a PowerPoint download link
manual-topic-engagements-share-a-powerpo.text: Figure 21. Share a PowerPoint download link. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Save a PPT Slidedeck to generate its presentation-specific code, then find the PPT Slidedeck card. 02 Use Copy link to paste its download URL into a message or document. The same control appears on the presentation edit page. 03 Use the QR image or PNG/SVG downloads in slides and handouts. Replacing the PowerPoint keeps these previously shared codes usable. Screenshot context: Copying a link or image does not add a visit. Opening the shared QR link records activity before delivering the file. Related chapters: People and organizations (p. 61) / Work queue (p. 77) / Chron and email (p. 89) / Map and calendar (p. 96)

manual-topic-engagements-select-and-orde.title: Select and order QR codes for a PDF
manual-topic-engagements-select-and-orde.text: Figure 22. Select and order QR codes for a PDF. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Expand Export Presentation and select View QR Codes PDF. Check one or more codes, or use Select all. 02 Drag any row by its handle, whether checked or unchecked. Only checked codes appear in the PDF, in list order from left to right and then top to bottom. 03 Keyboard users can focus a handle and use Up or Down to move a code. Select Prepare PDF to open the chosen sheet in a new tab, or Cancel to close the dialog. Screenshot context: PPT Slidedeck and Speaker Notes are selected and moved to the top. Other available codes remain below the visible rows. Related chapters: People and organizations (p. 61) / Work queue (p. 77) / Chron and email (p. 89) / Map and calendar (p. 96)

manual-topic-engagements-edit-presentati.title: Edit presentation details
manual-topic-engagements-edit-presentati.text: Figure 23. Edit presentation details. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Find the intended numbered presentation, check its topic and speaker, and enter the date, time, duration, and expected attendance. 02 Record actual attendance after the event. Zero is valid when nobody attended. 03 Continue to Presentation Files & QR Codes below these fields to add PDF notes and a PowerPoint file. 04 Use Save Changes in the persistent bottom bar to save the whole engagement form, including other edits on the page. Screenshot context: The retained illustration shows the same presentation fields; the current view and editor also number each presentation section. Related chapters: People and organizations (p. 61) / Work queue (p. 77) / Chron and email (p. 89) / Map and calendar (p. 96)

manual-topic-engagements-upload-or-repla.title: Upload or replace PDF notes and a PowerPoint
manual-topic-engagements-upload-or-repla.text: Figure 24. Upload or replace PDF notes and a PowerPoint. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 In the intended numbered presentation, choose a file or drop one onto Drop PDF here or Drop PowerPoint here. PPT Slidedeck accepts .ppt and .pptx. Choosing or dropping a file does not save it. 02 PDF files may be up to 100 MB and PowerPoint files up to 500 MB. Save Changes uploads files in small chunks. Watch the progress indicator, keep the page open, and wait for saving to finish. Interrupted chunks retry automatically. 03 Use Replace PDF or Replace PPT to select an updated file. The pending notice remains until you select Save Changes in the persistent bottom bar, which saves the entire engagement form. 04 To stop sharing a file, select its Remove current checkbox, review Removal pending, then Save Changes. Choose replacement or removal, not both. The existing QR link and statistics are retained. Screenshot context: Only upload files intended for the audience: anyone with the relevant QR link can open the notes or download the PowerPoint without signing in. The retained illustration shows the file controls; the current editor also provides separate PDF and PowerPoint drop areas. Related chapters: People and organizations (p. 61) / Work queue (p. 77) / Chron and email (p. 89) / Map and calendar (p. 96)

manual-topic-engagements-save-a-pending-.title: Save a pending presentation-file change
manual-topic-engagements-save-a-pending-.text: Figure 25. Save a pending presentation-file change. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Use Replace PDF or Replace PPT for a new file, or check Remove current PDF/PPT to remove the current one. Choose only one action for each file. 02 Read the pending notice. Selecting a file or checking Remove does not apply the change immediately. 03 Select Save Changes in the persistent bar at the bottom of the window. It saves the whole engagement form, including pending file changes. 04 After saving, verify the file details and sharing links. Leave without saving to keep the existing file. Screenshot context: Removal pending is illustrated with fictional speaker notes. The form was not saved and the file was kept. Related chapters: People and organizations (p. 61) / Work queue (p. 77) / Chron and email (p. 89) / Map and calendar (p. 96)

manual-topic-engagements-review-event-lo.title: Review event logistics

manual-topic-engagements-lifecycle-and-r.title: Lifecycle and rescheduling

manual-topic-engagements-review-combined.title: Review combined presentation QR activity
manual-topic-engagements-review-combined.text: Figure 28. Review combined presentation QR activity. manual-topic-engagements-draft-and-final.text: Figure 30. Draft and finalize received amounts. manual-topic-engagements-add-or-edit-reu.text: Figure 32. Add or edit reusable email text. manual-topic-organizations-contacts-orga.title: Organizations, Contacts, and Speakers
manual-topic-organizations-contacts-orga.text: Organizations hold relationship history, contacts identify the people involved, and speaker profiles keep presentation details and audience resources ready to reuse. Related chapters: Booking pipeline (p. 16) / Engagements (p. 26) / Chron and email (p. 89)

manual-topic-organizations-contacts-rela.title: Relationship Record
manual-topic-organizations-contacts-rela.text: Store the organization name, notes, affiliation, distinctives, website, phone, fax, and physical and mailing addresses. You can use one address for both or maintain them separately. Only the organization name is required; add address and relationship details when known. A new organization can create its first contact at the same time, and can add more contacts before saving.

manual-topic-organizations-contacts-pers.title: Person Record
manual-topic-organizations-contacts-pers.text: Store first and last name, optional primary organization, additional organization affiliations with their own roles or titles, email, phone, incidental notes, and an optional JPEG, PNG, or WebP photo up to 5 MB. A contact can be saved without an organization. Use Create Organization in the contact form to add a missing organization without losing the contact details or selected photo. The organization role is Pastor, Admin, or Other. When you choose Other, enter the custom description in Describe Other Role beside the Role field. Additional organizations each have their own role or title, such as Pastor at a church and Chairman at a research center. Event-specific roles are assigned separately on each engagement.

manual-topic-organizations-contacts-ente.title: Enter Organization Addresses
manual-topic-organizations-contacts-ente.text: • Choose the country before the region. The Country picker includes countries worldwide and defaults to United States of America for a new address. • For a United States address, the region field is labeled State and provides a dropdown of state names. • For a Canadian address, the region field is labeled Province and provides a dropdown of province and territory names. • For every other country, the field is labeled State/Province and accepts typed regional information. • The same behavior applies to both physical and mailing addresses. Select Same as Physical Address when the mailing address does not differ.

manual-topic-organizations-contacts-list.title: Lists, Details, and Financial History
manual-topic-organizations-contacts-list.text: • Search organizations by their details or active contacts; sort by name and switch between Active and Archived. • The organization list shows location, active contacts, Last Receipts, and Lifetime Receipts. Both receipt columns combine giving, lodging, travel, and book-table amounts from finalized reports. • Last Receipts uses the latest finalized event by event date; Lifetime Receipts includes all finalized history, including archived events. Drafts do not count toward either total. • An organization detail page summarizes lifetime giving, last and average event giving, lodging, travel, and recent finalized reports. • Search contacts by person or organization, sort by last name or organization, and choose 20, 50, or 100 records per page. • A contact detail page links to all its organizations and shows that person's Chron and open follow-up work.

manual-topic-organizations-contacts-choo.title: Choose a Profile, Contact, or Speaker Photo
manual-topic-organizations-contacts-choo.text: Use a JPEG, PNG, or WebP image up to 5 MB. Keep the face near the center: saved portraits use a centered square crop and appear in circular frames. The application creates compact list and detail images so contact directories and profile views load faster. Review the selected picture before saving. Choose a different source image if the crop cuts off important detail, or use the remove-picture option to return to the default portrait. Administrators can also update a user's picture from the user editor after unlocking sensitive actions.

manual-topic-organizations-contacts-keep.title: Keep Speaker Profiles Ready to Use
manual-topic-organizations-contacts-keep.text: Open Relationships > Speakers to find a speaker by name, email, or phone. Select Name to switch alphabetical order, then open the speaker's name or View icon for their details. Administrators and editors can use New Speaker or Edit Speaker; reviewers can view profiles and statistics. • Save the speaker's name, email address, and phone number once, then choose that speaker when adding presentations. • Add a biography and an optional photo to make the profile useful and recognizable. Photos can be JPEG, PNG, or WebP, up to 5 MB. • Add the speaker's website and other audience links. The written Bio is for the profile; Bio URL is the web page opened by the biography QR code. • For videos, social pages, or other resources, use Speakers > Edit Speaker > Custom Links. Give each link a clear name and full web address; select Add Custom Link for more, then Save speaker. Saving a new custom link adds a separate QR code to that speaker's existing presentations, and future presentations receive their own codes. Renaming or removing a profile link keeps already-published links and their statistics intact. To change or disable a shared code, select Statistics beneath that code on its presentation. Speakers cannot be archived. Administrators can delete unused speakers individually or with the selection checkboxes. Speakers referenced by presentations, short links, notes, or slide decks remain protected.

manual-topic-organizations-contacts-orga.title: Organization Archive Rule
manual-topic-organizations-contacts-orga.text: An organization cannot be archived while it still has active contacts, engagements, or inquiries. Archive those child records first, or move them to another active organization. Restoring a contact or engagement also requires its organization to be active.

manual-topic-organizations-contacts-find.title: Find Relationships in Large Lists
manual-topic-organizations-contacts-find.text: Organization and related-record selectors show bounded search results. If the item is missing, type a more specific name and use the search controls rather than assuming it was deleted. Validation summaries link to fields needing attention; correct those fields and save again.

manual-topic-organizations-contacts-chec.title: Check Similar Records Before Creating Another
manual-topic-organizations-contacts-chec.text: If a new contact or organization looks similar to an existing one, review the suggested matches before saving. Open the existing record if it is the same person or organization; confirm that yours is a distinct record only when it really is. A shared name alone does not prove that two records are the same. Administrators can review a contact or organization merge, choose the surviving record and field values, and confirm after checking the relationships that will move. The merge screen also offers Undo Merge for eligible merges for up to 90 days. Later changes to either record or its affected relationships can prevent undo. Ask an administrator to review a mistaken merge promptly.

manual-topic-organizations-contacts-birt.title: Birthdays and organization affiliations
manual-topic-organizations-contacts-birt.text: A contact can also store an optional birthday. Birthday-enabled calendar subscriptions create yearly all-day entries; they do not expose the birth year or internal contact notes. Additional affiliations are independent relationships, each with its own role or title. A contact can remain associated with another organization when one organization is removed. Event-specific assignments belong to each engagement.

manual-topic-organizations-contacts-sele.title: Select records for permanent deletion
manual-topic-organizations-contacts-sele.text: Administrators can use a row's individual Delete action or select checkboxes on Organizations, Contacts, Speakers, Engagements, Tasks, or Users and choose Delete selected. Editors and reviewers cannot delete records or access the selection controls. The selected count and Select all on this page apply only to displayed rows, up to 100. Clear selection resets the checkboxes. Changing pages or filters starts a new selection, so finish one page before continuing to another. Review the selected names and related data before confirming. Organization deletion can remove engagements and contacts that have no other organization; shared contacts are kept. Contact deletion removes affiliations, roles, tasks, and Chron. Engagement deletion removes its presentations, files, tasks, financial records, statistics, and Chron. Unused speakers can be deleted individually or in a group. Presentations, short links, notes, or slide decks protect a referenced speaker. Tasks are deleted without deleting their related record or standard task definition. Complete Admin Unlock if requested. The selection survives the redirect and expires after 30 minutes. The server rechecks the five-minute unlock at deletion time. After the Are you sure? dialog, the list reports how many selected records were deleted and how many were kept or failed. Review remaining items before retrying.

manual-topic-organizations-contacts-orga.title: Organization Receipt Totals
manual-topic-organizations-contacts-orga.text: Last Receipts and Lifetime Receipts on Organizations combine Giving Received, Lodging Received, Travel Received, and Book Table Received. Use the corresponding sort buttons to order the entire filtered directory by those same combined amounts; sorting remains consistent across pages. Last Receipts comes from the latest finalized event by event end date, then start date and event ID when dates tie. Lifetime Receipts includes every finalized event report, including archived event history. Drafts are excluded. No finalized history shows a dash for Last Receipts and $0.00 for Lifetime Receipts; confirmed zero remains $0.00. Older reports without a recorded book-table amount still contribute their recorded giving, lodging, and travel receipts.
