manual-topic-work-queue-work-queue.title: Work Queue
manual-topic-work-queue-work-queue.text: Tasks turn relationship context into an explicit next action with an owner, timing, priority, and state. They may stay attached to an Inquiry until selected work moves during booking. Related chapters: Daily dashboard (p. 13) / Engagements (p. 26) / Map and calendar (p. 96)

manual-topic-work-queue-my-reminders.title: My Reminders
manual-topic-work-queue-my-reminders.text: The sidebar badge and Dashboard personal cards always count your own reminders. In the queue, choose Mine, Everyone, or Unassigned; every queue summary count uses that same ownership scope, search, and related-record filter.

manual-topic-work-queue-queue-views.title: Queue Views
manual-topic-work-queue-queue-views.text: Choose an ownership scope, then filter Active, Overdue, Due Today, Next 7 Days, Waiting, or Completed. The Dashboard's My Overdue Work card opens Overdue limited to your assignments. Search matches task content, related records, and assignees.

manual-topic-work-queue-due-dates-and-ov.title: Due Dates and Overdue Pulses
manual-topic-work-queue-due-dates-and-ov.text: The due date appears as a short date, such as Sep 4, with a second line showing the number of days overdue, Due today, Due tomorrow, or Upcoming for later dates. Days are counted by calendar date in the application's time zone. Priority and workflow status appear separately. Active tasks more than 3 days overdue - starting at 4 days overdue - have a pulsing red row background. When several items qualify, the pulse moves down the list in a repeating cascade, with each pulse overlapping the next. Tasks 1-3 days overdue keep a steady red highlight; tasks due today have a blue highlight. Completed and canceled tasks do not pulse. The same attention cues appear in the Dashboard's My Work and Inquiry Next Actions lists. An active inquiry qualifies when its next-action due date is more than 3 days overdue. Hovering over a row, or moving keyboard focus to a control within it, shows an orange highlight over the pulse so you can clearly follow the item you are using. The pulse becomes visible again when the pointer and focus leave the row. If your device or browser prefers reduced motion, overdue items use a steady stronger red highlight instead of blinking.

manual-topic-work-queue-create-a-useful-.title: Create a Useful Task
manual-topic-work-queue-create-a-useful-.text: 01 Write a concrete title. Use notes for supporting detail, not as a substitute for the next action. 02 Link the right record. Search for an engagement, organization, or contact; choose General MOED work when no record applies. 03 Name an owner and due date. Tasks may be unassigned or have no date, but explicit ownership keeps them out of limbo. 04 Set priority and status. Choose Low, Normal, High, or Urgent and one of the workflow states below.

manual-topic-work-queue-fast-actions-and.title: Fast Actions and Record-Level Work
manual-topic-work-queue-fast-actions-and.text: The green check-mark icon opens Complete Task? and asks, "Are you sure you want to mark this task complete?" Select Complete Task to save the change, or Cancel or Esc to leave the task unchanged. This confirmation applies in the Work Queue and in record-level Follow-Up Work. From the queue, editors and administrators can assign an unowned task to themselves, start, complete, reopen, edit, or - administrators only - delete it. Engagement, organization, and contact detail pages show their open tasks in Follow-Up Work, where you can add a task or open a filtered queue. Administrators can also select the trash icon beside a task in Follow-Up Work, including on an engagement's Tasks tab. If admin actions are locked, complete the unlock workflow first, then select the trash icon again. Confirm Delete Task to permanently remove the task and return to the record. Deletion cannot be undone. Editors and administrators can select the Archive task box icon beside a task in Follow-Up Work or the Work Queue. Archiving removes it from active work, reminders, calendars, and digests while keeping its details and status. Use View Archived Tasks on the record or Archived in the Work Queue, then select Restore task to bring it back. Archived checklist tasks are retained when you add missing checklist tasks. Archiving an engagement or inquiry also hides its tasks from active work and reminders. Restoring the record brings back its Open, In Progress, and Waiting tasks. Completed, canceled, and individually archived tasks stay out of active work; all task details and statuses are preserved. Status Use It When What Happens Next Open The task is known but not started. Start it, complete it, or edit the owner/timing. In Progress Someone is actively working it. Complete it or move it to Waiting if blocked. Waiting Progress depends on a person, organization, or decision. The "Waiting on" description becomes required. Completed The action is finished. It moves to Completed and can be reopened. Canceled The action is no longer needed. It leaves active views and can be reopened.

manual-topic-work-queue-duplicate-a-task.title: Duplicate a Task to Another Event
manual-topic-work-queue-duplicate-a-task.text: 01 Open the task for editing. Select Duplicate to Another Event at the bottom of the Edit Task page. 02 Choose the destination event. In Search events, type at least three characters and choose a different event from the results. 03 Review the copied work. Adjust the copied title, notes, assignee, due date, and priority. The duplicate starts Open with "Waiting on" cleared. 04 Create the duplicate. Select Duplicate task. The new task is added to the destination event; the original is unchanged.

manual-topic-work-queue-standard-event-t.title: Standard Event Tasks
manual-topic-work-queue-standard-event-t.text: Standard tasks are reusable definitions copied when a new active engagement is first saved. Each has content, priority, display order, and a due date offset from event start or end. Administrators can select Also add this task to all active, open engagements when creating a definition, or Add to Active, Open Engagements afterward. This generates its checklist item for existing unarchived engagements with an Active lifecycle and open financial closeout. Each copy follows the definition's due-date rule and goes to the active Caller, or to the administrator if none is active. Existing copies, including completed and canceled tasks, are not duplicated. Initial standard tasks go to the selected Caller, or to the event creator when no Caller is selected. Changing the Caller later does not reassign these tasks; each remains independently editable. Changing an engagement's dates reschedules its active generated tasks from the standard schedule. A task whose due date was manually overridden keeps that date. Editing a standard definition does not rewrite an existing task's title, notes, priority, or current due date. Editors and administrators manage definitions in Standard Event Tasks. Add Missing Checklist Tasks creates absent standard items on an active engagement and assigns them to the acting user. The built-in financial closeout reminder is due one week after event end and cannot be edited, archived, or deleted. Sending a booking, reconfirmation, or thank-you message from an engagement does not complete its related checklist task automatically. Check the Correspondence result, then complete the task when the follow-up itself is finished.

manual-topic-work-queue-filter-work-and-.title: Filter Work and Update Several Tasks
manual-topic-work-queue-filter-work-and-.text: Use the ownership and status/date filters to focus the Work Queue. Applied filters stay visible and are remembered in this browser; use Clear Filters to widen the view if an expected task is missing. Open a task to review its owner, due date, and status. Waiting work should name what or whom you are waiting for. For event work, check the related event and any scheduling rule before changing the date. Editors and administrators can select eligible tasks and use Complete, Reassign, or Change Due Date. Choose Preview Updates, review the selected titles and proposed change, then apply it. Tasks that changed or became ineligible are skipped and reported. Bulk completion does not send checklist emails. Use an individual task's email action when correspondence is needed, and check its delivery status.

manual-topic-work-queue-archive-tasks-wi.title: Archive tasks without changing their status
manual-topic-work-queue-archive-tasks-wi.text: To archive a finished item, choose Completed or canceled in the Work Queue, then Archive task. In Archived, review both badges. Restore task retains details, status, owner, and due date; completed work stays completed. An open overdue task becomes eligible for reminders again when its engagement or inquiry is also unarchived.

manual-topic-work-queue-filter-and-selec.title: Filter and select work
manual-topic-work-queue-filter-and-selec.text: Figure 58. Filter and select work. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Choose My Tasks, Everyone's Tasks, or Unassigned Tasks. Apply status/date filters and review the visible filter summary. 02 Filters are remembered in this browser. Use Clear Filters to return to the default view. 03 Select tasks for a bulk update and review the planned changes before applying. Related chapters: Daily dashboard (p. 13) / Engagements (p. 26) / Map and calendar (p. 96)

manual-topic-work-queue-edit-a-task.title: Edit a task
manual-topic-work-queue-edit-a-task.text: Figure 59. Edit a task. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Choose or change a related record using the relationship picker. 02 Review owner, due date, priority, status, and Waiting On before Save Changes. Use Duplicate Task when separate follow-up is needed. Related chapters: Daily dashboard (p. 13) / Engagements (p. 26) / Map and calendar (p. 96)

manual-topic-work-queue-duplicate-a-task.title: Duplicate a task to another event
manual-topic-work-queue-duplicate-a-task.text: Figure 60. Duplicate a task to another event. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Choose Duplicate to Another Event from the task editor. 02 Search events and select a destination different from the source event. 03 Review copied title and notes, ownership, due date, priority, and status before saving. 04 The original task remains unchanged. Related chapters: Daily dashboard (p. 13) / Engagements (p. 26) / Map and calendar (p. 96)

manual-topic-work-queue-manage-reusable-.title: Manage reusable event checklists
manual-topic-work-queue-manage-reusable-.text: Figure 61. Manage reusable event checklists. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Editors and administrators open Work Queue > Standard Event Tasks to maintain the shared starting checklist. 02 Edit a definition's content, priority, display order, or due-date rule. Use + New Standard Task for another recurring item. 03 Archive a definition in Active to stop automatic creation for future events. Restore it from Archived to include it again. These changes apply to everyone creating events. 04 Existing event copies remain separate: archive an unnecessary copy in Follow-Up Work or the Work Queue. The required financial closeout reminder stays fixed at one week after event end. Related chapters: Daily dashboard (p. 13) / Engagements (p. 26) / Map and calendar (p. 96)

manual-topic-work-queue-schedule-a-stand.title: Schedule a standard task for existing engagements
manual-topic-work-queue-schedule-a-stand.text: Figure 62. Schedule a standard task for existing engagements. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Enter the reusable title and notes above the Scheduling section. Choose priority, date anchor, day offset, and display order. 02 Administrators can check Also add this task to all active, open engagements before Add standard task. Editors can maintain definitions but cannot use bulk generation. 03 This adds the task to unarchived engagements with an Active lifecycle and open financial closeout. Copies use the date rule and go to the active Caller, or to the administrator if none is assigned. 04 On a saved definition, administrators can use Add to Active, Open Engagements. Existing copies, including completed or canceled tasks, are kept without duplication. Screenshot context: The option is selected for illustration; the form was not submitted. Related chapters: Daily dashboard (p. 13) / Engagements (p. 26) / Map and calendar (p. 96)

manual-topic-work-queue-confirm-task-com.title: Confirm task completion
manual-topic-work-queue-confirm-task-com.text: Figure 63. Confirm task completion. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Select the check-mark Complete task action in the queue or a related record's task list. 02 Read Complete Task? and select Complete Task only when the work is finished. 03 Cancel or press Esc to return without changing the task. Screenshot context: The confirmation was canceled; no task was completed during capture. Related chapters: Daily dashboard (p. 13) / Engagements (p. 26) / Map and calendar (p. 96)

manual-topic-work-queue-restore-a-task-w.title: Restore a task with its original status
manual-topic-work-queue-restore-a-task-w.text: Figure 64. Restore a task with its original status. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Select Archived in the Work Queue, or View Archived Tasks from a related record. 02 Review the status badge as well as the Archived badge. This example remains Completed. 03 Select the curved-arrow Restore task control. Details, status, owner, and due date are retained. An open overdue task becomes eligible for active reminders again. Related chapters: Daily dashboard (p. 13) / Engagements (p. 26) / Map and calendar (p. 96)

manual-topic-work-queue-review-several-t.title: Review several task updates together
manual-topic-work-queue-review-several-t.text: Figure 65. Review several task updates together. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Select tasks and the bulk change, then preview. 02 Check each affected task, owner, status, and date. Apply Updates only when the review matches your intent. Related chapters: Daily dashboard (p. 13) / Engagements (p. 26) / Map and calendar (p. 96)

manual-topic-work-queue-understand-reusa.title: Understand reusable event task timing
manual-topic-work-queue-understand-reusa.text: Figure 66. Understand reusable event task timing. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Open a standard task to check its due rule, priority, and generated-work count. 02 Edits affect future copies. Existing event tasks remain independent; review them separately when timing changes. Related chapters: Daily dashboard (p. 13) / Engagements (p. 26) / Map and calendar (p. 96)

manual-topic-chron-mail-chron-and-email.title: Chron and Email
manual-topic-chron-mail-chron-and-email.text: Chron is the durable communication history. Add concise Chron Log Entries directly, send tracked engagement correspondence, or route copied inbound email into the relevant records. Related chapters: Booking pipeline (p. 16) / Engagements (p. 26) / Mattermost (p. 133)

manual-topic-chron-mail-use-the-chron-lo.title: Use the Chron Log
manual-topic-chron-mail-use-the-chron-lo.text: • Use Add Chron Log Entry on an inquiry, engagement, organization, or contact to save activity without editing the full record. Contact Chron records communication with that person only; Organization Chron records organization-level history; Engagement Chron records event-specific planning. • Entries show created time and author, newest first. Edited entries also show the last update time and editor. • Editors and administrators add, edit, and archive entries from the record's edit page. Administrators can permanently delete them. • Restore archived entries in batches from the Restore page. An archived parent record must be active before its Chron can be restored. • Email-generated entries link to their retained inbound or outbound source message while it exists.

manual-topic-chron-mail-start-from-an-en.title: Start from an Engagement
manual-topic-chron-mail-start-from-an-en.text: Open an active engagement and select Send Message. Choose assigned contacts or speakers as To, Cc, or Bcc recipients, and optionally use Cc Me or Bcc Me for your account email. To and Cc addresses are visible; Bcc addresses stay hidden. Review the message, then queue it. The engagement marker and related Chron history are handled for you. Check the Correspondence section for the result.

manual-topic-chron-mail-route-outside-em.title: Route Outside Email
manual-topic-chron-mail-route-outside-em.text: When using another mail application, copy the inbound address and keep the exact engagement marker in the subject or plain-text body: [DNR#123.<signed-token>]. Use the copy icon beside the marker on the engagement page.

manual-topic-chron-mail-how-inbound-emai.title: How Inbound Email Finds Its Records
manual-topic-chron-mail-how-inbound-emai.text: Reading a message in your mail application does not prevent MOED from importing it. Importing leaves the original message and its read/unread state unchanged. If older mail is missing after mailbox setup or recovery, ask the deployment operator to review historical mail; marking it unread will not trigger an import. One unique, valid signed engagement marker routes directly to that active engagement only when the sender also uniquely matches an active record. Unknown senders and unsigned legacy markers require review. When participant matching is uncertain, only the signed engagement receives the Chron entry.

manual-topic-chron-mail-address-matching.title: Address Matching
manual-topic-chron-mail-address-matching.text: MOED matches exact email addresses for active verified users, contacts, and organizations. A unique contact participant routes to the Contact and its Organization. A direct organization address routes there. Cc and Bcc delivery both work.

manual-topic-chron-mail-what-inbound-mai.title: What Inbound Mail Retains
manual-topic-chron-mail-what-inbound-mai.text: The Chron entry includes normalized headers, subject, timestamps, inert plain-text body, attachment names, and a source link. Attachment contents are not stored. Duplicate delivery of the same message ID is ignored.

manual-topic-chron-mail-review-the-inbou.title: Review the Inbound Queue
manual-topic-chron-mail-review-the-inbou.text: Editors and administrators see messages grouped as Needs review, Pending, Processing, Failed, Processed, or Rejected. Without a valid signed marker, every message requires review. Unknown or ambiguous senders, shared addresses, messages with no unique target, and invalid, conflicting, unknown, or archived engagement markers also require review. 01 Inspect the source. Open Inbox in the sidebar. On a wide screen, the message list is on the left, the reader is in the middle, and the filing panel is on the right. Search by subject, sender, or content; use Order and the queue pages to find a message. Needs review starts oldest first. Selecting a message keeps Search messages visible at the same vertical position. Expand Message details for recipients, sent time, and attachment names, or Routing details for matching reasons. On a phone, use Back to messages to return to the list. 02 Choose the Chron Logs. In the filing panel, review the reason under Review needed. Select the intended Contact, Organization, or Inquiry suggestions when available. Find an active engagement by name, ID, or email marker and choose it from the Engagement list. Check the count of selected Chron logs before saving. 03 Choose an outcome. Save to Chron logs saves the conversation to the selected records. Find matches again checks routing again after record corrections. Expand Other actions to Reject message while retaining the source without writing Chron. For a processed message, review Message status and Saved to Chron to confirm where it was filed.

manual-topic-chron-mail-treat-address-ma.title: Treat Address Matching as a Routing Aid
manual-topic-chron-mail-treat-address-ma.text: An exact visible From address is not independent proof of identity. Respect the mailbox provider's spam and SPF/DKIM/DMARC signals. Leave suspicious messages for review. Administrators can expand Manage retained email below the reader and choose Purge Mail Entry after confirmation. Purge removes the retained MOED mail card and source links, but preserves Chron entries and never deletes the original IMAP message.

manual-topic-chron-mail-review-recipient.title: Review Recipients, Message, and Follow-Up
manual-topic-chron-mail-review-recipient.text: The engagement email composer separates recipient choices, the message, and reply follow-up into cards. Choose an active template or Custom Message, then review each selected contact or speaker and its To, Cc, or Bcc setting. The copy-to-yourself choice is separate. Review the message and the optional event brief before Queue Email. Correspondence shows what was queued and its delivery result. To track a reply, select Create a Task to Review the Reply in Reply Follow-Up and check the Follow-Up Date. The task belongs to you. Receiving a reply does not complete it; review the correspondence before marking it complete. In Inbox, read the message and check the filing panel before saving it to Chron logs. The divider separates the reader from the filing choices; on narrow screens, use the page's navigation to return to the message list.

manual-topic-chron-mail-email-delivery-s.title: Email delivery states and retries
manual-topic-chron-mail-email-delivery-s.text: Queued messages can be Pending or Processing before becoming Sent, Failed, Delivery Uncertain, or partially delivered across recipients. Open the delivery record to inspect individual recipient outcomes and timestamps. Retry Failed Deliveries retries the failures rather than re-sending successful recipients. Correct a bad destination before retrying. Inquiry delivery retries are available while the inquiry is active. Delivery Uncertain means the message may already have arrived. Check the provider reference or recipient first; only then acknowledge the review and use Retry Reviewed Deliveries. After booking conversion, replies to earlier inquiry email route into the resulting engagement. The original inquiry retains the pre-booking record and any tasks not moved. The Inbox filing panel saves an email to existing destinations. Create a new booking request from New Inquiry in Booking Pipeline when needed, then return to the Inbox and review the appropriate destinations.

manual-topic-chron-mail-read-mail-and-hi.title: Read mail and historical mailbox review
manual-topic-chron-mail-read-mail-and-hi.text: MOED tracks new mailbox messages independently of read or unread flags. Reading a message in your mail client does not prevent its import, and importing does not alter the original message or its read state. The first mailbox scan, or recovery after a mailbox identity reset, can hold unfamiliar historical messages for operator review. Marking an older message unread does not request another import. Ask the deployment operator to review pending historical mail and import or skip it deliberately. The README appendix contains the reconciliation commands. Use Inbox to route a message after it has been imported.

manual-topic-chron-mail-archive-and-rest.title: Archive and restore Chron in batches
manual-topic-chron-mail-archive-and-rest.text: Open the parent record's edit/Chron controls to archive an obsolete entry. Archive preserves history; administrator-only deletion removes it permanently after fresh confirmation. Open Restore Archived Chron Log Entries, select the entries to return, and choose Restore Selected. The parent must be active. Restored entries retain their historical authorship and dates.

manual-topic-chron-mail-add-a-chron-entr.title: Add a Chron entry
manual-topic-chron-mail-add-a-chron-entr.text: Figure 67. Add a Chron entry. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Use Add Chron Log Entry to record a decision without opening the complete edit form. 02 Include the context, outcome, and agreed next step. 03 Save the entry; its author and time appear in reverse chronological history. Related chapters: Booking pipeline (p. 16) / Engagements (p. 26) / Mattermost (p. 133)

manual-topic-chron-mail-compose-an-email.title: Compose an email and plan reply follow-up
manual-topic-chron-mail-compose-an-email.text: Figure 68. Compose an email and plan reply follow-up. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Choose an active template or Custom Message. 02 In Reply Follow-Up, choose Create a Task to Review the Reply and check Follow-Up Date. The task is assigned to you; receiving a reply does not complete it. 03 Review recipients and message before Queue Email. Saving a browser draft does not send. Related chapters: Booking pipeline (p. 16) / Engagements (p. 26) / Mattermost (p. 133)

manual-topic-chron-mail-review-recipient.title: Review recipient visibility and sender copies
manual-topic-chron-mail-review-recipient.text: Figure 69. Review recipient visibility and sender copies. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Choose To, Cc, or Bcc for each selected person. To and Cc are visible; Bcc is hidden. 02 Set Your Copy separately. Check the message and optional share-safe event brief before queueing. Related chapters: Booking pipeline (p. 16) / Engagements (p. 26) / Mattermost (p. 133)

manual-topic-chron-mail-review-copied-in.title: Review copied inbound email
manual-topic-chron-mail-review-copied-in.text: Figure 70. Review copied inbound email. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Open Inbox in the sidebar. Use Needs review, Pending, Processing, Failed, Processed, Rejected, or All to choose a queue. 02 Search by subject, sender, or message content. Change Order or use the queue pages when needed. Needs review starts oldest first. 03 On a wide screen, the message list is on the left, the reader is in the middle, and the filing panel is on the right. 04 Select a message to read it. Search messages stays visible at a consistent vertical position. On a phone, use Back to messages to return to the queue. Related chapters: Booking pipeline (p. 16) / Engagements (p. 26) / Mattermost (p. 133)

manual-topic-chron-mail-read-an-inbound-.title: Read an inbound message beside its filing choices
manual-topic-chron-mail-read-an-inbound-.text: Figure 71. Read an inbound message beside its filing choices. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Choose a message in Inbox. The divider separates the reader from Message Filing. 02 Read the message, review selected Chron logs, and correct destinations before Save to Chron Logs. Related chapters: Booking pipeline (p. 16) / Engagements (p. 26) / Mattermost (p. 133)

manual-topic-map-calendar-map-and-calend.title: Map and Calendar
manual-topic-map-calendar-map-and-calend.text: Use the map for geographic planning, the graphical month calendar for events and due work, and private subscription links for an external calendar application. Related chapters: Engagements (p. 26) / Work queue (p. 77) / Profile and security (p. 124)

manual-topic-map-calendar-engagement-map.title: Engagement Map
manual-topic-map-calendar-engagement-map.text: The initial view shows active engagements in a bounded date window. Filter by lifecycle, confirmation, and date. Pin colors show confirmation, with lifecycle shown by the outline or symbol. Select a pin for the event, organization, dates, lifecycle, and a link to details. Use Fit visible pins after filtering. The companion list includes On map, Needs address, Awaiting lookup, and Not located views for the current page, with Edit location links. Find missing addresses searches the selected date and lifecycle scope; Previous and Next reach additional pages. A new address may take time to resolve.

manual-topic-map-calendar-monthly-calend.title: Monthly Calendar
manual-topic-map-calendar-monthly-calend.text: The Calendar page opens to the current month. On a desktop, scroll up or down inside the calendar to see consecutive weeks across month boundaries, such as late October beside early November. More weeks and their items load as you scroll; weekday headings stay visible. Use Previous or Next to show the complete month before or after the month named in the heading. Today returns to the current month from its first week. The current day has its own rose-colored cell and Today badge, distinct from every event and task color. Your content filter stays selected while you browse. If more weeks cannot load, use Retry loading weeks or try the month controls again. Select an event to open its details. Tasks with due dates link to task work; editors and administrators return to the same calendar view after editing.

manual-topic-map-calendar-private-calend.title: Private Calendar
manual-topic-map-calendar-private-calend.text: Create a separate subscription for each device or service. The secret URL is shown only once; copy it or open it directly in a calendar app. Choose Events, Presentations, My Active Work, All Active Work, and/or Birthdays (from Contacts) for each link. All Active Work includes everyone's due-dated active tasks and disables My Active Work. Events, Presentations, and Birthdays are selected by default. Revoke one link without affecting the others. Revoked token records can be purged. Share a subscription URL only with the intended device or calendar service: it grants access to the selected schedule, task titles, and contact birthday names. Internal Chron, travel, lodging, and compensation are excluded.

manual-topic-map-calendar-choose-what-th.title: Choose What the Month Calendar Shows
manual-topic-map-calendar-choose-what-th.text: Selector Calendar Content Color Coding Events Engagements that overlap the displayed dates. Event color, with distinct border tones for tentative/postponed, canceled, and completed events. My Tasks Your active tasks that have a due date in the displayed calendar grid. Your task accent color. All Tasks Every active due-dated task in the grid, including unassigned work. Your tasks use the accent color; other or unassigned tasks use a contrasting color. Birthdays Annual birthday reminders from active contacts. Birthday styling; open the contact for details. Everything Events, all active due-dated tasks, and contact birthdays. Event, task, and birthday colors appear together. On a phone, the calendar becomes a daily agenda with previous/next day controls and Today. The selected filter remains active as you move between dates. The summary above the grid reports how many matching events and tasks fall in that month.

manual-topic-map-calendar-understand-the.title: Understand the Map Provider
manual-topic-map-calendar-understand-the.text: The map uses Amazon Location when it is configured for the installation; otherwise the supported OpenStreetMap-based view remains available. Attribution identifies the actual provider. Expand map credits when needed. Date, lifecycle, confirmation, and location filters still control the same engagement records. An unavailable tile service is different from an event with a missing or unresolved address.

manual-topic-map-calendar-apply-map-filt.title: Apply Map Filter Changes
manual-topic-map-calendar-apply-map-filt.text: When you change a map filter, the highlighted Apply Filters control reminds you that the map is still showing the previous selection. Apply the change, then use Fit Visible Pins if needed. Check the missing-address or unlocated lists for records that cannot appear as pins. Clear filters before assuming an event has disappeared.

manual-topic-map-calendar-choose-the-con.title: Choose the content of each private feed
manual-topic-map-calendar-choose-the-con.text: Each new subscription has a Device or Service label and one or more content options: Events, Presentations, My Active Work, All Active Work, and Birthdays (from Contacts). The defaults are Events, Presentations, and Birthdays. My Active Work includes assigned work; All Active Work includes everyone and unassigned work. Active work appears on its due date. A subscription can therefore reveal task titles and schedule context: share it only with the intended device or service. The private URL is shown only once. Save it immediately or create a new subscription if it is lost. Revoke one link without changing others, and purge revoked token records when no longer needed. The in-app month selector and a private feed are separate controls. Changing the month selector does not change the saved subscription content.

manual-topic-map-calendar-correct-a-map-.title: Correct a map location
manual-topic-map-calendar-correct-a-map-.text: Use Edit location to correct the written event address. If the address is right but the lookup pin is wrong, open the pin editor, choose the intended coordinates, and save the manual confirmation. A manual override is tied to the address it confirms. Check it again after changing the address. Clear the override to return to normal address lookup. The map/list can still show an event awaiting lookup or without enough address information.

manual-topic-map-calendar-birthdays-and-.title: Birthdays and the mobile daily agenda
manual-topic-map-calendar-birthdays-and-.text: The month selector includes Birthdays. Everything includes events, active due-dated work, and birthdays. Enter contact birthdays as MM/DD; a birth year is not collected. February 29 birthdays recur on the last day of February in non-leap years. On a phone-sized display the calendar becomes a daily agenda. Use the previous/next day controls or Today, keep the desired content selector, and open the linked record. Desktop uses the month grid. The agenda and month view preserve the chosen content scope.

manual-topic-map-calendar-amazon-locatio.title: Amazon Location and Map Fallback
manual-topic-map-calendar-amazon-locatio.text: Configured deployments use Amazon Location maps; otherwise the supported OpenStreetMap-based view remains available. Expand the collapsed attribution/credits to identify the active provider. Date, lifecycle, confirmation, missing-address, pending-lookup, and unlocated-record controls retain their existing meaning. Fit Visible Pins adjusts the viewport; Edit Location changes the record location. Provider configuration belongs to the operator, not to the event location form.

manual-topic-map-calendar-locate-engagem.title: Locate engagements
manual-topic-map-calendar-locate-engagem.text: Figure 72. Locate engagements. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Filter the date window, lifecycle, and confirmation state. 02 Select a pin for event context; use Fit visible pins after filtering. 03 Use the list views to find missing addresses, pending lookups, or unlocated records, then Edit location. Related chapters: Engagements (p. 26) / Work queue (p. 77) / Profile and security (p. 124)

manual-topic-map-calendar-confirm-an-eve.title: Confirm an event pin
manual-topic-map-calendar-confirm-an-eve.text: Figure 73. Confirm an event pin. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Check the written event address before changing a pin. 02 Zoom and click the map, drag the pin, or enter latitude and longitude. 03 Check the venue confirmation, then Save confirmed pin. Use automatic lookup clears an override. 04 A later address change requires checking the pin again. Related chapters: Engagements (p. 26) / Work queue (p. 77) / Profile and security (p. 124)

manual-topic-map-calendar-browse-the-mon.title: Browse the month calendar
manual-topic-map-calendar-browse-the-mon.text: Figure 74. Browse the month calendar. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Scroll inside the desktop calendar to browse consecutive weeks across months. Previous and Next show the complete adjacent month named relative to the heading; Today restores the current month from its first week. 02 Choose Events, My Tasks, All Tasks, Birthdays, or Everything. 03 Tasks need an active status and a due date to appear. 04 Click an event, task, or birthday to open its record. The rose Today cell is separate from event/task colors. Screenshot context: The retained illustration shows one month. The current desktop calendar also scrolls continuously, loading adjacent weeks and their items; the phone view remains a daily agenda. Related chapters: Engagements (p. 26) / Work queue (p. 77) / Profile and security (p. 124)

manual-topic-reimbursements-reimbursemen.title: Reimbursements
manual-topic-reimbursements-reimbursemen.text: Record expenses, review receipts, and submit a complete package to the bookkeeper. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Administration (p. 138)

manual-topic-reimbursements-record-expen.title: Record Expenses
manual-topic-reimbursements-record-expen.text: Enter the date, merchant, amount, and account. Upload, paste, or photograph the receipts, then save.

manual-topic-reimbursements-build-a-draf.title: Build a Draft
manual-topic-reimbursements-build-a-draf.text: Select your available expenses, set the request dates, and check the totals and receipt filenames.

manual-topic-reimbursements-review-and-s.title: Review and Submit
manual-topic-reimbursements-review-and-s.text: Check the recipients, email, and ZIP package. Confirm when ready, then follow the delivery history.

manual-topic-reimbursements-after-submis.title: After Submission
manual-topic-reimbursements-after-submis.text: The request, expenses, and receipts are locked. Submitted is not a payment status. Check Email Delivery for email progress and coordinate corrections with the bookkeeper. Archive keeps the original package and history.

manual-topic-reimbursements-reimbursemen.title: Reimbursements at a Glance
manual-topic-reimbursements-reimbursemen.text: Use Reimbursements in the sidebar to record your own expenses, attach receipts, and send a reviewed request to the bookkeeper. Start with + Add Expense; select available expenses to create a draft; open Requests to review and submit it. Payment tracking stays in the bookkeeper's system. Editors and administrators can create and edit their own expenses and drafts. Reviewers have read-only access to their own records. Administrators can view other owners and manage shared settings, but viewing another owner does not permit changing or submitting that person's expenses. Submitted expenses stay locked.

manual-topic-reimbursements-add-an-expen.title: Add an Expense and Receipts
manual-topic-reimbursements-add-an-expen.text: 01 Open Reimbursements > + Add Expense. Enter Expense Date, Merchant or Payee, Amount (USD), and Account. Add a useful Description or Purpose. 02 Use Upload Receipt, drop files into the receipt area, select Paste Image, or use Take a Receipt Photo where available. If clipboard permission is denied, focus the paste area and use your normal paste shortcut. 03 Check the selected filenames, count, and size. Remove a staged file if it is wrong. Select Save Expense to store the expense and selected files. Selecting a file alone does not upload it. JPEG, PNG, WebP, and PDF are supported. An expense may have up to 20 receipts and 15 MB of receipt files in total. If a save fails, check the message; files may need to be selected again. A duplicate warning is advisory. If another tab changed the expense, reload and reconcile your changes before saving again.

manual-topic-reimbursements-find-and-sel.title: Find and Select Expenses
manual-topic-reimbursements-find-and-sel.text: Use Search Expenses, date filters, Active/Archived views, and sort controls to narrow the list. Administrators default to their own Expense Owner and can deliberately choose another owner or All Users. Open a row to view its expense; icons expose permitted View, Edit, Archive/Restore, and Delete actions. Only your available active expenses can be included in a new draft. Draft and submitted entries are already assigned; submitted rows are light green. Use Select All Available to select eligible expenses across all pages of the current filters, or select individual checkboxes. Review the selected count, total, and missing-receipt count, and use Clear Selection above or below the list to start over. Selection can span pages in the same browser tab; changing filters clears it.

manual-topic-reimbursements-create-and-e.title: Create and Edit a Draft Request
manual-topic-reimbursements-create-and-e.text: 01 Select available expenses. Expand Dates for New Request if the proposed request dates need changing; these dates are separate from browsing filters. 02 Select Create Draft Request from Selected Expenses. It is disabled until an eligible expense is selected. 03 Open the draft and select Edit Draft. Use Request Date Range > Update Dates, Add an Expense in This Date Range > Add Expense, or Remove beside an included expense. The date range must cover all included expenses. 04 Check Download Report PDF or Download Package ZIP, then select Review and Submit. Removing an expense or deleting an eligible draft request keeps the expense and its receipts. Deleting an expense is a separate administrator action. Saving, editing, or downloading a draft does not send it.

manual-topic-reimbursements-review-and-s.title: Review and Submit a Reimbursement
manual-topic-reimbursements-review-and-s.text: 01 From the Requests list, use the Submit icon beside your eligible draft reference, or open it and select Review and Submit. 02 Review Email Details, Email Preview, Submission Readiness, and Package Contents. The bookkeeper is To; the owner, personal reviewer, and settings Cc address receive Cc copies. The settings Bcc address receives a hidden copy. 03 Check the amounts and exact receipt filenames. The ZIP contains the expense report PDF, an expense CSV, and original receipts. Missing receipts are flagged; pending or rejected required security checks block submission. 04 Select I Have Reviewed the Recipients, Email, and Package, then Submit Reimbursement Request. If details changed after preview, review the refreshed content before trying again. Submission changes the request to Submitted and locks its expenses and receipts. Email delivery runs separately. Submitted does not mean paid, and Accepted by SMTP does not prove that the recipient read the email.

manual-topic-reimbursements-track-delive.title: Track Delivery and Handle Corrections
manual-topic-reimbursements-track-delive.text: Open a submitted request to inspect Email Delivery and Request History. Known failures offer Retry Failed Delivery; accepted, uncertain, or cancelled copies may offer Send Another Copy. Read the history, check with the recipient/provider, enter a reason, and confirm before sending again. An uncertain copy may already have arrived. Record a Correction saves a reason and cancels only copies that have not started sending. It cannot recall email or unlock submitted expenses. After agreement with the bookkeeper, use Resolve Correction and record the resolution. Neither action submits a replacement. Recovery uses the original approved message and package for up to 365 days; older messages may lack a recoverable snapshot. Use the original package and contact the bookkeeper if recovery is unavailable.

manual-topic-reimbursements-download-rep.title: Download Reports and Match Receipts
manual-topic-reimbursements-download-rep.text: Download Submitted Package returns the original ZIP that was sent. The submitted PDF download comes from that same package. Later profile, account, settings, or template changes do not rewrite the original. Older records without a saved original package show an explanation rather than silently generating a substitute. The report includes account subtotals, Total Amount Due, and Expense Detail. Each detail entry names its matching receipt files, including the expense number and amount. The Receipt Files index lists PDF and image originals; PDF receipt pages and image previews in the report do not replace the originals in the ZIP's receipts/ folder.

manual-topic-reimbursements-manage-the-c.title: Manage the Chart of Accounts
manual-topic-reimbursements-manage-the-c.text: Editors and administrators open Chart of Accounts from Reimbursements or Requests. Search by COA number or description; choose Active, In Use, or Archived; sort by COA Number, Description, or Expenses in either direction. Use Add Account, Edit, Archive, or Restore as appropriate. COA numbers must be unique even among archived accounts. Administrators may delete unused accounts; accounts linked to expenses must be archived instead. An expense may keep its previously assigned archived account, but new assignments must use an active account.

manual-topic-reimbursements-to-bookkeepe.title: To: Bookkeeper
manual-topic-reimbursements-to-bookkeepe.text: The bookkeeper email in Reimbursement Setup receives the request for processing.

manual-topic-reimbursements-cc-visible-c.title: Cc: Visible Copies
manual-topic-reimbursements-cc-visible-c.text: The submitting user, personal reviewer, and setup Cc address receive copies, when configured.

manual-topic-reimbursements-bcc-hidden-c.title: Bcc: Hidden Copy
manual-topic-reimbursements-bcc-hidden-c.text: The setup Bcc address receives a hidden copy and is excluded from recipient-visible report content. Administrators open Reimbursement Setup in the sidebar. Set the organization name, bookkeeper first/last name, bookkeeper email and phone, Cc Email Address, and Bcc Email Address; save with administrator actions unlocked. The Bcc address is not printed in recipient-visible reports or email bodies. Each user can open My Profile > Personal Details, set Reimbursement Reviewer Email, and save the profile. This person receives a Cc copy when that user submits. Verify the actual recipients on every submission preview. Settings changes affect new submissions, not previously approved messages.

manual-topic-reimbursements-review-the-r.title: Review the Request and Its Downloads
manual-topic-reimbursements-review-the-r.text: Follow the four steps at the top: Select Expenses, Review Request, Review Email, and Submit. The count and total help you check the current selection. Select All Available includes eligible expenses across pages within the browsing filters; check the selection before creating the draft. Browsing filters and the new request's date range serve different purposes. In the draft, add an optional Note to the Bookkeeper and save it before reviewing the email. Expense links open a read-only detail view; use Edit Expense when it is yours and still editable. A submitted request locks its expenses and receipts. Download the report PDF or package ZIP when available; the CSV is inside the ZIP. The email carries one ZIP containing the PDF, CSV, and original receipts. The CSV has one row per expense. The PDF includes receipt previews, including supported PDF receipt pages; the original files remain in the ZIP. Match receipt filenames to the report's receipt list. On Review Reimbursement Email, verify recipients, note, amounts, and package contents. The size gauge shows usage of the 18 MB ZIP limit. The line below checks the complete encoded email against 25 MB, including message, headers, and encoding. A request also allows up to 100 receipts and 15 MB of original files. Reduce large receipts or split the request if it is over a limit. After submitting, wait for the progress message instead of clicking repeatedly. Check the request's delivery result afterward; Submitted does not mean paid.

manual-topic-reimbursements-screen-refer.title: Screen Reference: Expenses
manual-topic-reimbursements-screen-refer.text: Open Reimbursements from Work in the sidebar. + Add Expense opens entry; Requests opens the request register; Chart of Accounts opens the shared account list for editors and administrators. Search Expenses matches the available expense search fields; use Start Date, End Date, and Apply to set the browsing range. Administrator Expense Owner defaults to the signed-in user; All Users is an explicit choice. Active and Archived switch visibility. Date, Merchant, Owner, Account, Amount, and Status sorting toggle direction; page-size and pagination controls limit displayed rows. The table shows Include, Date, Merchant / Payee, Owner where permitted, Account, Receipts, Amount, Status, and Actions. Hovering a row reveals its view link; explicit icons and links remain usable. Available means unclaimed and eligible for the current owner; Draft or Submitted links to its request. Submitted rows are green. The mobile disclosure exposes additional owner/account/receipt detail. Include checkboxes are available only for the signed-in owner's active unclaimed expenses. Create Draft Request from Selected Expenses appears above and below the list. Selected count, amount, and missing-receipt count reflect selections across pages in this tab; filtering or successful creation clears stale selection. Clear Selection appears at both ends when applicable. Dates for New Request exposes Request Start Date and Request End Date independently of list filters. Server validation rechecks every selection. View opens an expense without edit controls. Edit is limited to the owner's editable expense. Archive and Restore preserve the record; Delete is administrator-only and requires confirmation and current administrator unlock. Expenses associated with requests have additional restrictions: submitted items are locked and draft items are managed through their request.

manual-topic-reimbursements-screen-refer.title: Screen Reference: Expense Entry and Detail
manual-topic-reimbursements-screen-refer.text: Expense Date, Merchant or Payee, Amount (USD), and Account are required. Description or Purpose provides supporting context. Choose an Account lists active chart-of-accounts entries; an existing archived assignment may be retained. Amounts are stored in integer cents. Save Expense saves all fields and staged receipts; Back to Expenses or Back to Request returns to the originating context. Expense Receipts accepts Upload Receipt, the drop area, Paste Image, the keyboard paste area, and Take a Receipt Photo when the device supports it. A camera prompt depends on browser/device support. Clipboard reads may require a user gesture and permission; keyboard paste is the fallback. New picks append to staged files; review filename, count, and byte totals and remove unintended selections before saving. An expense allows 20 receipts with 15 MiB combined originals, and each receipt must also satisfy the 15 MiB limit. Formats: JPEG, PNG, WebP, PDF. The saved Receipts pane shows image or first-page PDF previews, filenames, Open Original Receipt, and Delete Receipt where permitted. Preview failure does not by itself mean that the original is missing. Original downloads require authorization. If scanning is enabled, queued/scanning/rejected files cannot be previewed, downloaded, or submitted until they are clean; installation status determines whether scanning is required. Rejected files should be replaced with a safe original. Delete Expense is outside the Receipts pane and deletes the whole eligible expense and its receipts. Delete Receipt removes only that attachment. Both require the applicable permissions and confirmation; submitted records expose neither mutation. Expense History records changes. Duplicate detection is an advisory; version conflicts reject stale saves and preserve text values. File inputs may need reselecting after errors. Repeated creation with the same save token does not create duplicate expenses.

manual-topic-reimbursements-screen-refer.title: Screen Reference: Requests Register
manual-topic-reimbursements-screen-refer.text: Open Requests from Reimbursements. Search Requests accepts a request reference or owner search; administrators can filter Owner. Status offers All Statuses, Draft, or Submitted. Expense Dates From and Through filter overlapping request date windows. Sort By offers Created, Submitted, Total, Owner, and Request; Direction chooses ascending or descending. Apply refreshes the list. Active/Archived and pagination retain the selected context. Columns are Request (hash and readable request number), Owner, Expense Dates, Expenses, Receipts, Total, Status, Status Set, and Actions. Status Set is the creation time for Draft and submission time for Submitted; this screen currently labels these timestamps UTC. Submitted rows are green. Hover/click opens a read-only view; the View icon does the same. The paper-plane Submit icon appears only for the signed-in owner's eligible active draft. Edit opens that draft. Archive/Restore changes visibility, preserving record links and locks. Delete is available only for an eligible draft with the required role; an administrator cannot delete a submitted request to free its expenses.

manual-topic-reimbursements-screen-refer.title: Screen Reference: Request View and Edit
manual-topic-reimbursements-screen-refer.text: The header identifies owner, date range, and status. Download Report PDF and Download Package ZIP are available when items exist; submitted requests use Download Submitted Package. Expenses, Back to Requests, Chart of Accounts, Edit Draft, and Review and Submit appear according to role, ownership, state, and view mode. Back to Requests preserves an allowed originating list URL. Edit Draft places Request Date Range and Add an Expense in This Date Range in equal-width panels that stack on narrow screens. Set Start Date and End Date and choose Update Dates. The range must encompass every included expense. Available Expense contains the owner's eligible unclaimed expenses inside that range; choose one and Add Expense. The add panel is absent when none are available. Expenses lists Date, Merchant / Payee, Account, Receipt Files, Amount, and Remove in editable drafts. Merchant links always open permitted read-only expense detail. Remove frees that expense from the draft without deleting its receipt files. Total Amount Due sums the items. Delete Request sits directly on the page background; it removes only the draft and preserves its expenses and receipts. Submitted views add delivery summary/history, correction controls for authorized users, and Request History. Archive does not cancel mail or unlock content. Reviewers cannot edit; editors and administrators cannot change another owner's expense content merely because it is visible.

manual-topic-reimbursements-screen-refer.title: Screen Reference: Email Review and Submission
manual-topic-reimbursements-screen-refer.text: Review Reimbursement Email shows Email Details (subject and recipients), a readable Email Preview in either app theme, Submission Readiness, and Package Contents. Check each listed expense, amount, receipt count, scan state, filename, and original-file size. Missing receipts are advisory; unresolved required security checks, configuration errors, or oversized packages prevent submission. To is the configured bookkeeper. Cc includes the submitting owner, optional Reimbursement Reviewer Email, and optional Cc Email Address. Bcc Email Address receives a hidden copy. Recipient addresses are validated and duplicate routing is resolved by the application; the preview is the authoritative list. Bcc recipients are absent from recipient-visible report content. The message uses the MOED email header and footer. The attached ZIP includes the Expense Report PDF, CSV, and every original receipt in receipts/. It is the same package represented by the download. Each receipt filename begins with expense and receipt identifiers; the report's Expense Detail and Receipt Files sections match those names. Image receipt pages are convenient previews; PDF receipt pages are embedded in the report where supported; PDFs and images also remain separate original files in the ZIP. A request is limited to 100 receipts and 15 MiB of originals; the finished ZIP has an 18 MB limit and the complete encoded email has a 25 MB limit. Base64 email encoding adds roughly one third plus headers. Split a large request or reduce source image sizes before review. Select I Have Reviewed the Recipients, Email, and Package, then Submit Reimbursement Request. The app rechecks the review fingerprint, records the original package, queues delivery, sets Submitted, and locks the associated content. Merely opening the preview sends nothing.

manual-topic-reimbursements-screen-refer.title: Screen Reference: Delivery Recovery and Correction
manual-topic-reimbursements-screen-refer.text: Email Delivery distinguishes Pending/Queued, Sending, Retry, Accepted by SMTP, Failed, Delivery Uncertain/Needs Review, and Cancelled. It lists recipient type/address when retained, attempts, and last acceptance. Exact labels may describe the worker state rather than the request state. Submitted means the request was recorded and locked; it does not mean delivered, read, approved, or paid. Retry Failed Delivery applies to known failures. Send Another Copy applies to accepted, uncertain, or cancelled copies when the approved snapshot is available, the request is active, and no correction remains unresolved. Enter a reason, confirm you have checked the prior delivery, and confirm sending. Recovery reuses the original approved recipient, message, and package; changing settings does not redirect that copy. Never repeatedly resend an uncertain copy without checking whether it arrived. Record a Correction requires a reason. It keeps the submitted record and expense links, records the actor/time, and cancels pending/retry copies only. Sending, accepted, and uncertain copies cannot be recalled. Resolve Correction requires a Resolution Note documenting agreement with the bookkeeper. It neither sends mail nor unlocks an expense. Coordinate replacements externally to avoid duplicate reimbursement. Exact-message recovery is retained for 365 days. Some legacy records have no approved-message snapshot or original package; the UI explains what is unavailable. Downloaded originals are immutable, including any historical formatting. Request History records submission, archive, correction, and recovery actions. The app does not track payment status.

manual-topic-reimbursements-screen-refer.title: Screen Reference: Chart of Accounts
manual-topic-reimbursements-screen-refer.text: Editors and administrators can open Chart of Accounts. Add Account or Edit Account contains required COA Number (up to 20 characters) and Description (up to 120). Save/Add persists the entry; Cancel abandons edit mode. The COA number is globally unique across active and archived entries. The list provides Search Chart of Accounts, Active/In Use/Archived, and ascending/descending sort on COA Number, Description, or Expenses. In Use means active accounts referenced by at least one expense. Each row shows those values and Edit, Archive/Restore, and administrator Delete icons where allowed. Search/sort/view context is preserved while editing. Delete requires an unused account, confirmation, and administrator unlock. Archive is the safe way to retire an account with history.

manual-topic-reimbursements-screen-refer.title: Screen Reference: Reimbursement Setup and Profile
manual-topic-reimbursements-screen-refer.text: Reimbursement Setup is administrator-only in the sidebar. Organization Name identifies the report/email organization. Bookkeeper First Name and Last Name personalize the recipient; Bookkeeper Email Address is the destination; Bookkeeper Phone Number appears in the report context. Cc Email Address adds a visible copy; Bcc Email Address adds a hidden copy. Save Reimbursement Setup requires current administrator unlock. Validation errors preserve entries. Saved settings apply to future submissions. My Profile > Personal Details includes Reimbursement Reviewer Email, an optional personal Cc recipient. Save the profile to persist it. The verified account email also receives a copy. The reviewer field is independent of recovery-email verification and does not grant the reviewer application access. The app records reviewer-setting changes without exposing the address in the audit message.

manual-topic-reimbursements-reimbursemen.title: Reimbursement Troubleshooting and Access
manual-topic-reimbursements-reimbursemen.text: No Include checkbox or a disabled Create Draft Request button: check that the expense is yours, active, unclaimed, and selected. A dash for a Draft/Submitted expense protects it from inclusion twice. Administrator All Users visibility does not transfer ownership. No Submit/Edit icon: confirm the request is your active draft and that you have an editor or administrator role. Submitted and archived requests are not editable drafts. A missing Add Expense panel means no eligible available expense is in that request's date range. Paste Image fails: use the button after copying an image, allow browser permission if prompted, or use the focused paste area and normal keyboard shortcut. Pasted text is not a receipt. Save Expense is still required. If files fail size/type checks, keep valid selections and remove or replace the rejected file. Delivery is queued indefinitely or reports a development transport: ask the deployment administrator to verify the real SMTP worker and transport; changing the request to another draft is not a delivery fix. Accepted by SMTP is not a receipt. For uncertain delivery, check the recipient/provider before any intentional resend. Cannot modify a submitted expense or receipt: this is an intentional content lock. Record a correction and coordinate with the bookkeeper. Chart-of-accounts edits and profile changes do not rewrite the original PDF. Original package missing on a legacy record: preserve the received package if available and contact the administrator; do not submit the same expenses again.

manual-topic-reimbursements-expenses-sav.title: Expenses, saved selection, and workflow progress
manual-topic-reimbursements-expenses-sav.text: Figure 78. Expenses, saved selection, and workflow progress. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Follow Select Expenses, Review Request, Review Email, and Submit at the top. 02 Apply owner/date/state filters and check the current summary. View opens read-only detail; Edit returns through the allowed expense list. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Administration (p. 138)

manual-topic-reimbursements-select-avail.title: Select available expenses across pages
manual-topic-reimbursements-select-avail.text: Figure 79. Select available expenses across pages. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Choose Select All Available to include eligible expenses across pages of the current filters. 02 Check selected count, total, and missing-receipt count. Changing filters clears selection; Clear Selection starts over. 03 Review Dates for New Request before Create Draft Request from Selected Expenses. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Administration (p. 138)

manual-topic-reimbursements-enter-expens.title: Enter Expense Details
manual-topic-reimbursements-enter-expens.text: Figure 80. Enter Expense Details. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Enter Expense Date, Merchant or Payee, Amount (USD), Account, and Description or Purpose. 02 Use an active account for a new assignment. An existing expense can retain its previously assigned archived account. 03 Continue to Expense Receipts below these fields, then select Save Expense. Only the owner can edit an eligible expense. Screenshot context: Fictional documentation records. The screen continues below the illustrated area. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Administration (p. 138)

manual-topic-reimbursements-attach-and-r.title: Attach and Review Receipts
manual-topic-reimbursements-attach-and-r.text: Figure 81. Attach and Review Receipts. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Use Upload Receipt, drag-and-drop, or Paste Image; on supported phones, the camera option captures a photo. If clipboard access is blocked, use the keyboard paste shortcut or upload. 02 Select Save Expense to store selected files. The Receipts panel shows saved previews and original filenames; select a receipt to open the original. 03 Supported formats are JPEG, PNG, WebP, and PDF. Each expense allows at most 20 receipts totaling 15 MB. Submitted receipts stay locked. Screenshot context: Scrolled expense editor. Preview is a fictional PDF receipt; the original remains downloadable. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Administration (p. 138)

manual-topic-reimbursements-find-draft-a.title: Find Draft and Submitted Requests
manual-topic-reimbursements-find-draft-a.text: Figure 82. Find Draft and Submitted Requests. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Open Requests. Filter by search text, owner, status, and expense dates; choose sort field and direction, then Apply. 02 Switch between Active and Archived. The request identifier or hovered row opens its detail view. 03 Use the available Submit, View, Edit, Archive, Restore, or protected Delete actions. Eligibility and ownership determine which actions appear; submitted rows use light green. Screenshot context: Fictional documentation records. The screen continues below the illustrated area. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Administration (p. 138)

manual-topic-reimbursements-edit-dates-e.title: Edit dates, expenses, and a bookkeeper note
manual-topic-reimbursements-edit-dates-e.text: Figure 83. Edit dates, expenses, and a bookkeeper note. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Save the optional Note to the Bookkeeper before reviewing the email. 02 Use Update Dates, Add Expense, or Remove as needed. Removing an expense preserves its original receipts. 03 Download Report PDF or Download Package ZIP for review, then Review and Submit. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Administration (p. 138)

manual-topic-reimbursements-read-expense.title: Read expense details and preview a PDF receipt
manual-topic-reimbursements-read-expense.text: Figure 84. Read expense details and preview a PDF receipt. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Expense links open read-only details and receipt previews. 02 Open Original Receipt for the complete file. Choose Edit Expense only when you own the editable expense. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Administration (p. 138)

manual-topic-reimbursements-review-the-e.title: Review the email and ZIP attachment
manual-topic-reimbursements-review-the-e.text: Figure 85. Review the email and ZIP attachment. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Check To, Cc, Bcc, and the readable Email Preview, including your saved note. 02 Only one ZIP is attached; it contains the report PDF, expense CSV, and original receipts. Download it before submitting. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Administration (p. 138)

manual-topic-reimbursements-check-packag.title: Check package contents and both email limits
manual-topic-reimbursements-check-packag.text: Figure 86. Check package contents and both email limits. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 The gauge shows usage of the 18 MB ZIP limit. The encoded email, including headers and message, must also fit within 25 MB. 02 Match the PDF, CSV, and original receipt filenames to the expense list. The request also limits original files to 15 MB and 100 receipts. 03 Check I Have Reviewed the Recipients, Email, and Package, then Submit Reimbursement Request. Wait for progress and check delivery afterward; Submitted does not mean paid. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Administration (p. 138)

manual-topic-reimbursements-check-delive.title: Check Delivery and Record Corrections
manual-topic-reimbursements-check-delive.text: Figure 87. Check Delivery and Record Corrections. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Open a submitted request and inspect Email Delivery for each recipient. Queued, failed, uncertain, or accepted delivery is separate from reimbursement payment. 02 For a known failure, use Retry Failed Delivery where offered. Before Send Another Copy, review prior delivery and check whether it already arrived; a duplicate may otherwise be sent. 03 Expand Record a Correction to record an issue, then coordinate with the bookkeeper. Corrections keep original records locked; Resolve Correction records the agreed outcome. Screenshot context: The fictional request is queued in an isolated environment with no mail worker. No email was sent. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Administration (p. 138)

manual-topic-reimbursements-search-and-m.title: Search and Manage the Chart of Accounts
manual-topic-reimbursements-search-and-m.text: Figure 88. Search and Manage the Chart of Accounts. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Use Add Account with a unique COA Number and Description. Archived accounts still reserve their numbers. 02 Search the Chart of Accounts, then choose Active, In Use, or Archived. Sort COA Number, Description, or Expenses in either direction. 03 The table below offers Edit, Archive, and Restore as appropriate. Only administrators can delete unused accounts; accounts associated with expenses must be archived. Screenshot context: Fictional documentation records. The screen continues below the illustrated area. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Administration (p. 138)

manual-topic-reimbursements-set-organiza.title: Set Organization and Shared Recipients
manual-topic-reimbursements-set-organiza.text: Figure 89. Set Organization and Shared Recipients. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Administrators open Reimbursement Setup and enter Organization Name and the bookkeeper name, email, and phone. 02 Set Bcc Email Address for a hidden copy and Cc Email Address for a visible shared copy. Check the resulting recipients on each submission review. 03 Select Save Reimbursement Setup and complete administrator confirmation when requested. Changes affect drafts and future submissions, not saved original packages. Screenshot context: Fictional documentation records. The screen continues below the illustrated area. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Administration (p. 138)

manual-topic-reimbursements-set-your-per.title: Set Your Personal Reimbursement Reviewer
manual-topic-reimbursements-set-your-per.text: Figure 90. Set Your Personal Reimbursement Reviewer. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Open My Profile from the sidebar and find Personal Details. 02 Enter Reimbursement Reviewer Email. This address receives a Cc copy of requests you submit and is separate from your account email. 03 Select Save Changes below the profile panels. Verify the actual recipients again before submitting a reimbursement. Screenshot context: Personal Details crop from the current profile screen, with fictional example.org addresses. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Administration (p. 138)

manual-topic-reimbursements-pdf-receipt-.title: PDF receipt pages within the report
manual-topic-reimbursements-pdf-receipt-.text: Figure 91. PDF receipt pages within the report. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 This page is rendered from the actual fictional request report. The receipt heading identifies its expense, amount, account, original filename, and PDF page. 02 Review embedded receipt pages alongside Expense Detail and Receipt Files. The original receipt and CSV remain inside the ZIP. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Administration (p. 138)

manual-topic-profile-security-profile-an.title: Profile and Security
manual-topic-profile-security-profile-an.text: Your profile makes ownership recognizable; the security controls protect your identity and provide safe recovery paths. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Map and calendar (p. 96) / Administration (p. 138) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-profile-security-profile-an.title: Profile and Notifications
manual-topic-profile-security-profile-an.text: Maintain your name, phone, optional profile picture, and notification schedule. Use the separate Change Recovery Email panel to verify a new address; the current recovery address remains active until verification succeeds. Successful verification signs out all sessions and pauses the daily digest. Resending verification preserves the profile draft and chosen photo; disabled digest schedules do not require a delivery time or day. A verified email enables password recovery and a Dashboard-style Daily Digest of upcoming engagements, My Work, event readiness, and financial closeouts. Overdue and due-today tasks are highlighted, and editor/admin digests also include inbound mail awaiting review. The digest defaults to enabled on weekdays at 7:00 a.m.; disable it or choose a different time and set of days at any time. To adjust Daily Digest delivery, open My Profile and find Notification Preferences. Dashboard and record links in the message remain available.

manual-topic-profile-security-password-r.title: Password Rules
manual-topic-profile-security-password-r.text: To change your own password, open Account Security in the sidebar, then find Change Password. Enter Current Password, New Password, and Confirm New Password, then select Change Password. Use at least 12 characters and no more than 72 UTF-8 bytes. Other sessions are signed out. If prompted, sign in with two-factor authentication again. The Change Recovery Email form on My Profile changes the recovery address, not your password. A temporary password must be replaced before using other areas.

manual-topic-profile-security-set-up-two.title: Set Up Two-Factor Authentication
manual-topic-profile-security-set-up-two.text: Two-factor authentication is required for Administrators, Editors, and Reviewers. Complete setup when prompted at sign-in, then save your recovery codes. 01 Confirm your password. If replacing an existing authenticator, also enter a current code. 02 Add the account. Scan the QR code in your authenticator app or enter the manual setup key. 03 Verify enrollment. Enter the six-digit code generated by the app. 04 Save recovery codes. Each code works once and the page will not show them again. Store them in an approved password manager or another secure location. At sign-in, enter either the current six-digit authenticator code or one unused recovery code. Generating new recovery codes invalidates all old ones. Every account type must keep 2FA enabled. If your account does not have an authenticator yet, your next successful password login will open setup before you can access the application. New invitations and accounts whose 2FA was reset follow the same setup process. Existing password-only sessions must sign in again.

manual-topic-profile-security-recover-ac.title: Recover Access
manual-topic-profile-security-recover-ac.text: • Forgotten password: choose "Forgot your password?" on sign-in and enter the verified email on the active account. The single-use link lets you set a new password and invalidates existing sessions. • Lost authenticator: use one saved recovery code at the 2FA prompt, then replace the authenticator and generate a fresh set of codes. • No recovery factor: contact an administrator. They can issue a temporary password or reset another user's 2FA after elevated confirmation; they cannot reveal an old password or recovery code. • New account: open the invitation link within seven days, create a private password, and complete required authenticator enrollment.

manual-topic-profile-security-choose-a-r.title: Choose a Reimbursement Reviewer
manual-topic-profile-security-choose-a-r.text: In My Profile > Personal Details, set Reimbursement Reviewer Email and save. The address receives a Cc copy of your reimbursement submission. It is separate from your verified account/recovery email, and entering it does not create a MOED login.

manual-topic-profile-security-change-the.title: Change the recovery email securely
manual-topic-profile-security-change-the.text: Use the separate Change Recovery Email panel. Enter the new address, current password, and a fresh authenticator code when 2FA is enabled, then select Verify New Email Address. The current address stays in use while the new address is pending. Follow the verification message sent to the new address to finish. Successful verification signs out all sessions and pauses the daily digest. Sign in again and review notification preferences. Cancel Pending Email Change abandons a pending request. Resend email verification requests a new message while preserving the profile draft and chosen photo. Editing the ordinary profile form does not directly replace the recovery destination.

manual-topic-profile-security-manage-you.title: Manage your personal profile
manual-topic-profile-security-manage-you.text: Figure 92. Manage your personal profile. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Open My Profile from your name at the bottom of the sidebar. Update your name, phone, or optional picture. 02 Use JPEG, PNG, or WebP for a photo, then review the crop before saving. The maximum upload is 5 MB. 03 The recovery email is displayed here. Use the separate Change Recovery Email form to verify a new address. 04 Scroll to Notifications to choose Daily Digest delivery time and days, then select Save Changes. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Map and calendar (p. 96) / Administration (p. 138) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-profile-security-choose-dai.title: Choose Daily Digest time and days
manual-topic-profile-security-choose-dai.text: Figure 93. Choose Daily Digest time and days. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Open My Profile and scroll to Notifications. Enable Daily work digest to receive the Dashboard summary by email. 02 Choose Delivery time in the displayed business timezone and select the days. Weekdays, Weekends, and Every day provide shortcuts. 03 Select Save Changes. Delivery starts at the selected time; the mail worker may send a few minutes later. 04 To change delivery settings later, return to My Profile. The email footer contains plain text; Dashboard and record links remain available in the message. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Map and calendar (p. 96) / Administration (p. 138) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-profile-security-manage-acc.title: Manage account security
manual-topic-profile-security-manage-acc.text: Figure 94. Manage account security. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Every account type must use 2FA. Accounts without it enroll at their next successful password login. Replace the authenticator from Account Security when needed. 02 Change your password with the current password and required factor. 03 Generate fresh recovery codes when needed; save them securely because each works once. 04 Administrator resets and password changes can invalidate other sessions. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Map and calendar (p. 96) / Administration (p. 138) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-profile-security-start-auth.title: Start authenticator replacement
manual-topic-profile-security-start-auth.text: Figure 95. Start authenticator replacement.
