Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Confirm your password and, when replacing an enrolled factor, your current authentication code. 02 Scan the enrollment QR code in an authenticator or enter its setup key. 03 Enter the generated six-digit code to verify enrollment, then store the recovery codes. Screenshot context: Only the initial confirmation screen is illustrated. Enrollment secrets and recovery codes are intentionally absent. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Map and calendar (p. 96) / Administration (p. 138) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-profile-security-verify-a-n.title: Verify a new recovery email
manual-topic-profile-security-verify-a-n.text: Figure 96. Verify a new recovery email. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 In Change Recovery Email, enter the new address, then the current password and a fresh authenticator code when required. 02 Select Verify New Email Address, then follow the verification message at the new address. 03 Your old address stays active until verification. The change signs out all sessions and pauses the digest. 04 Cancel a pending change or resend verification from My Profile if needed. Screenshot context: The retained illustration shows the earlier field arrangement. The current form places the new address on its own row, with the password and authenticator code below it. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Map and calendar (p. 96) / Administration (p. 138) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-profile-security-sign-in-to.title: Sign in to MOED
manual-topic-profile-security-sign-in-to.text: Figure 97. Sign in to MOED. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Enter the username and your private password. 02 Complete the required authenticator or recovery-code challenge. If your account is not enrolled yet, complete authenticator setup before accessing the application. 03 If prompted to change a temporary password or enroll an authenticator, complete that step before continuing. 04 Use the account menu to sign out when finished. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Map and calendar (p. 96) / Administration (p. 138) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-profile-security-request-pa.title: Request password recovery
manual-topic-profile-security-request-pa.text: Figure 98. Request password recovery. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Choose Forgot your password? on sign-in. 02 Enter the verified email address on the active account and request a reset link. 03 Follow the single-use link to choose a new password. Existing sessions are invalidated. 04 If no verified email or recovery factor is available, contact an administrator. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Map and calendar (p. 96) / Administration (p. 138) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-mattermost-mattermost.title: Mattermost
manual-topic-mattermost-mattermost.text: The MOED plugin brings daily summaries, engagement context, follow-up actions, and carefully reviewed engagement email into Mattermost while MOED remains the system of record. Related chapters: Engagements (p. 26) / Work queue (p. 77) / Chron and email (p. 89)

manual-topic-mattermost-link-your-accoun.title: Link Your Account First
manual-topic-mattermost-link-your-accoun.text: Open Mattermost in MOED and generate a one-time code. The code is shown once, expires after 10 minutes, and becomes invalid after use. In Mattermost, run /moed connect CODE. Command responses are private to you. Never paste the code into an ordinary channel message.

manual-topic-mattermost-commands.title: Commands
manual-topic-mattermost-commands.text: Command What It Does Who Can Use It /moed help Shows the command reference and account-linking reminder. Everyone /moed status Checks the plugin connection and reports which MOED account is linked. Everyone /moed connect CODE Consumes a one-time code from the MOED Mattermost page and links your identities. Everyone /moed today Shows a private dashboard with Overdue, Due today, Next 7 days, and Waiting counts, active assigned tasks, and a link back to MOED. Linked users /moed tasks Shows the same task dashboard with up to 15 active tasks assigned to you. Editors and administrators also receive permitted action buttons. Linked users /moed event search TEXT Searches active and historical non-archived engagements by event or organization name. Linked users /moed event show ID Shows a private engagement card with dates, status, location, work counts, and an email routing marker you can copy. Linked users /moed link-event ID Binds the current channel to an engagement, adds its routing marker to the channel name, and posts its card. Editors and administrators with native channel-management and posting permission /moed unlink-event Removes the channel's engagement binding and its channel-name marker. Editors and administrators with native channel-management and posting permission

manual-topic-mattermost-engagement-cards.title: Engagement Cards
manual-topic-mattermost-engagement-cards.text: Run /moed event show ID for a private engagement card. Linking a channel posts the same useful engagement context for the channel. Both cards show the email routing marker with a Copy control so it can be kept in a related email subject or message. Use Open in MOED for the complete record.

manual-topic-mattermost-task-buttons.title: Task Buttons
manual-topic-mattermost-task-buttons.text: Editors and administrators can assign an unowned task to themselves, start it, complete it, or reopen it. Each button checks the task version before changing MOED; if someone already changed the task, refresh with /moed tasks. Waiting details, reassignment to someone else, editing, cancellation, and deletion remain in MOED.

manual-topic-mattermost-recognize-the-en.title: Recognize the Engagement Linked to a Channel
manual-topic-mattermost-recognize-the-en.text: On desktop and mobile, a linked channel's sidebar label begins with a compact marker such as [MOED#17], leaving more room for the channel title. The full signed routing marker remains available in engagement cards and email tools wherever it is needed for routing. The colored chain control provides the same link signal; select it, or choose MOED engagement from the channel menu, to see the engagement, open it in MOED, copy its routing marker, or begin an email. Unlinking removes the marker from the channel name.

manual-topic-mattermost-send-engagement-.title: Send Engagement Email from Mattermost
manual-topic-mattermost-send-engagement-.text: 01 Start from the right engagement. In a linked channel, select the MOED chain icon and choose Send MOED email. To include a particular conversation, open that post's Message actions and choose Send via MOED email. 02 Choose a starting point. Select an active template from the shared Email Templates library, or Custom message, then choose from the contacts already assigned to the engagement. To include an assigned speaker, use the engagement email composer in MOED. Each unique address receives a separate message. 03 Decide what to include. Edit the subject and message. You may append the share-safe event brief and, when you started from a post, the selected post or a short thread excerpt. 04 Review before sending. Check the recipients, routing marker, subject, message, and any added context on the review screen. Nothing is sent until you choose Send and add to Chron. 05 Confirm the result. The form shows whether each delivery is pending, sent, or failed and links to the full delivery record in MOED. The message is also recorded in the Engagement, Organization, and selected Contact Chron logs. 06 Watch for replies. When a marked reply is routed back to the engagement, the MOED bot privately notifies the Mattermost user who most recently emailed that person about the engagement. Open the notification to continue in the engagement Chron.

manual-topic-mattermost-turn-a-mattermos.title: Turn a Mattermost Post into MOED Work
manual-topic-mattermost-turn-a-mattermos.text: 01 Link the channel. An editor or administrator runs /moed link-event ID. The link establishes which engagement receives work from that channel. 02 Open Message actions. Hover over a channel post and choose Message actions using the grid/apps icon - not the three-dot menu. Then choose Add MOED task, Add to MOED Chron, or Send via MOED email. 03 Review before saving or sending. Confirm the task, Chron entry, or email details in the form. Nothing changes in MOED and no email is sent until you submit the final review. 04 Continue in MOED. The resulting task, Chron entry, or email delivery record appears on the linked engagement, with the selected Mattermost context when you chose to include it.

manual-topic-mattermost-create-follow-up.title: Create Follow-Up Work
manual-topic-mattermost-create-follow-up.text: Add MOED task creates follow-up work on the engagement linked to the channel. MOED suggests a title and notes from the post. Review them, choose a due date and priority if needed, then save. The task appears with the engagement's other work in MOED.

manual-topic-mattermost-preserve-context.title: Preserve Context as History
manual-topic-mattermost-preserve-context.text: Add to MOED Chron adds the post to the linked engagement's history. Review or edit the suggested entry, then choose Save to Chron. Use this for decisions, outcomes, commitments, and useful conversation context that should remain with the engagement.

manual-topic-mattermost-continue-the-con.title: Continue the Conversation
manual-topic-mattermost-continue-the-con.text: Send via MOED email creates a reviewed message to assigned engagement contacts. You can include the selected post or a short thread excerpt, and MOED keeps the routing marker, delivery result, and Chron history together.

manual-topic-mattermost-read-the-receipt.title: Read the Receipt Reactions
manual-topic-mattermost-read-the-receipt.text: • Chron Chron receipt: the MOED bot adds the :memo: reaction after Add to MOED Chron successfully writes the selected post to the linked engagement. • Email Email receipt: the MOED bot adds the :email: reaction when a MOED email includes the selected post or thread and at least one recipient delivery succeeds. • Both may appear: the reactions are independent, so one post can show both. They are visual receipts rather than counters; MOED remains the authoritative record. • New actions only: reactions appear for Chron saves and email deliveries completed after this feature is deployed. Earlier Chron entries and emails are not marked retroactively.

manual-topic-mattermost-before-you-save.title: Before You Save
manual-topic-mattermost-before-you-save.text: Task, Chron, and email actions all show what will be saved or sent. They are available in channels linked to a MOED engagement when your account has permission. Opening, reviewing, or canceling a form changes nothing.

manual-topic-mattermost-permissions-priv.title: Permissions, Privacy, and Unlinking
manual-topic-mattermost-permissions-priv.text: • MOED decides access: linking does not grant a new role. Reviewers stay read only; editors and administrators receive only the task actions their MOED role permits. • Private by default: personal summaries, searches, email forms, delivery results, reply alerts, errors, and action confirmations are visible only to the requesting user. link-event deliberately posts a channel-visible engagement card, including its routing marker and Copy control. • MOED is authoritative: task, Chron, and email actions use MOED's permissions, delivery service, and records. The plugin does not connect to the MOED database or keep a second copy of engagement email. • Post actions are scoped: the plugin verifies that you can read the selected post and obtains the engagement from the channel's link. MOED permits task, Chron, and email actions only for linked editors and administrators. • Remove access: open Mattermost in MOED and choose Unlink. The Mattermost account immediately loses command access until it is linked again.

manual-topic-mattermost-connect-moed-and.title: Connect MOED and Mattermost
manual-topic-mattermost-connect-moed-and.text: Figure 99. Connect MOED and Mattermost. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 When configured, generate a one-time linking code here and run /moed connect CODE in Mattermost. 02 Use /moed today, /moed tasks, and event search/show for private context. 03 Editors and administrators may link channels and review task, Chron, and email actions. 04 Unlink an account here to revoke its Mattermost command access. Screenshot context: The disposable preview is not connected to Mattermost. The chapter explains the configured plugin workflow; this screen shows its setup prerequisite. Related chapters: Engagements (p. 26) / Work queue (p. 77) / Chron and email (p. 89)

manual-topic-administration-administrati.title: Administration
manual-topic-administration-administrati.text: Administrator tools control identity, accountability, continuity, and deployment health. Use them deliberately and keep a second administrator available. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Troubleshooting (p. 157) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-administration-review-ai-co.title: Review AI Coach Requests
manual-topic-administration-review-ai-co.text: Administrators can open ai coach Requests under Administration in the sidebar when the coach is enabled. The log shows each question and originating page, the requesting user and role, the date and time, the result and response duration, and the administrator's assessment. Completed describes processing, not a guarantee that the answer was correct. 01 Find a request. Use Search questions or corrections and the Assessment filter, then select Filter. Open the linked question to inspect its original answer, manual sources, user feedback, and page or walkthrough context. 02 Record the assessment. Under Review and correction, choose an Assessment, describe what worked or needs improvement, and add Correct step-by-step guidance if you have verified it. Start from the user's page, name the next visible control, and explain how to confirm success. Select Save review. 03 Choose the follow-up. The original response is preserved. The administrator assessment is separate from the user's helpful or needs work rating. Saving review notes alone does not replace future answers. Use Create improvement case for guidance that should be checked and reused, or Guidance improvements to inspect the wider review queue.

manual-topic-administration-turn-coach-f.title: Turn Coach Feedback into Verified Improvements
manual-topic-administration-turn-coach-f.text: On ai coach Improvements, the Feedback review queue collects ratings, missing-control reports, failed answers, and responses taking more than 15 seconds. Related requests are grouped for investigation; a group does not imply that every question needs the same answer. Recent development reviews records completed investigations as Fixed, Verified, or Deferred with a summary and date. 01 Create a case from evidence. Open a request and select Create improvement case, or select New improvement on the improvements page. Remove names and private record details from the Question. Select the category, user role, page, guided step, and expected workflow that apply. 02 Verify the correct guidance. Follow the real application controls and check the Comprehensive Manual. Enter Verified expected guidance. Use Find current Comprehensive Manual topic IDs to locate source topics. Add required or forbidden words or phrases where they will help detect a recurring error. 03 Save a draft or approve. Keep the Status as Draft while investigating. To approve, choose Approved and confirm both that you checked the current application and manual and that the case contains no private information. Select Save improvement. Approved guidance can be reused for a matching question in the same role, page, and guided-step context. 04 Recheck after changes. When the application guidance changes, an approved case can show Needs revalidation. Recheck and approve it before its answer can be reused. Export approved test cases downloads reviewed cases for development regression checks; redact private details before approval and export. The improvement process is to investigate a real request, verify the intended workflow, correct the manual or application guidance, and test the result. Development reviews are performed by the maintainer or a separately configured review automation. The queue itself does not run a development agent, publish changes, or retrain the language model.

manual-topic-administration-delete-an-ai.title: Delete an AI Coach Request
manual-topic-administration-delete-an-ai.text: Administrators can select Delete beside an entry in ai coach Requests, or Delete request on its detail page. Review the identified request, then select Delete request to confirm or Cancel to keep it. Deletion permanently removes that question, its answer, feedback, review notes, and corrections. Linked improvement cases are kept. If the request is still being answered or has changed since confirmation, reload it before trying again. Deleting an entry does not clear the whole log, end an open conversation, or train the model.

manual-topic-administration-clear-the-ai.title: Clear the AI Coach Request Log
manual-topic-administration-clear-the-ai.text: On the request list, select the red Clear request log button and review the number of entries in the confirmation. The final Delete entries button includes that count; select it to confirm or Cancel to keep the log. This permanently removes the requests included in the confirmation and their answers, review notes, and corrections for all users, regardless of the current search or assessment filter. Requests still being answered and newly submitted requests are kept. Improvement cases and development-review records are preserved. Clearing the log does not clear anyone's open conversation or change the model; new requests continue to be recorded.

manual-topic-administration-users.title: Users
manual-topic-administration-users.text: , or when a sensitive action directs you to confirmation, enter your administrator password plus a fresh authenticator or recovery code. Select Unlock Sensitive Actions to return to the requested page. Locked user controls appear after confirmation succeeds. The Administrator actions unlocked banner shows the remaining time beside Automatically locks in. Unlock starts with five minutes in the current signed-in session; select Add 5 Minutes in the banner while it is unlocked to extend the deadline. The countdown updates to the new deadline; another administrator or browser session does not inherit it. Moving between pages preserves the current deadline. At expiry the banner disappears and the server requires a new unlock for sensitive actions. Deactivating or deleting users preserves the current deadline without restarting the countdown. Select Admin Unlock under Administration to unlock before choosing a sensitive action and return to your current page. Select Lock Admin Actions in the center of the orange banner to end the unlock immediately while staying signed in. Protected delete and sensitive-action confirmations check your current session first. If it is locked, complete Confirm Administrator Access, then select the action again to review its confirmation. Users Invite a username, verified-on-acceptance email, and Reviewer, Editor, or Admin role. Review account status, profile, email verification, 2FA, password-change requirement, and activity timestamps. Each user card shows the Daily Digest delivery days and whether delivery is off or paused. Use Edit after unlocking administrator actions to review its time, time zone, and days; users can also adjust their own Notification Preferences in My Profile. Elevated actions can resend invitations, edit profile details, username, role, and daily work digest settings, set a temporary password, reset another user's 2FA, deactivate/activate, or delete an invited or inactive account. Deactivation revokes sessions and calendar links and unassigns tasks; activation does not restore those links or assignments.

manual-topic-administration-audit-log.title: Audit Log
manual-topic-administration-audit-log.text: Inspect login, security, and database-change activity with actor, affected record, IP address, and local time. Filter by category, text, date range, and exact IP. Entries are newest first and append-only during normal use; individual records cannot be edited or deleted. In the Retention panel, administrators choose how many days to keep and preview the exact local cutoff and affected count. Pruning requires freshly confirmed administrator access, the literal PRUNE phrase, and a final themed in-app confirmation. The completed operation is recorded in the log.

manual-topic-administration-encrypted-ba.title: Encrypted Backup
manual-topic-administration-encrypted-ba.text: The encrypted backup includes application records and uploaded files, including PDF Speaker Notes, PPT Slidedecks, and profile, contact, and speaker photos. The backup page shows current files, retained replacements, and storage health. Ask your administrator to resolve any storage warning before relying on a new backup. Confirm the administrator password and a fresh factor, then choose and confirm a unique backup password of at least 16 characters. MOED downloads the encrypted snapshot as a .dnrbackup file. While the export runs, the page shows Creating Encrypted Backup and asks you to keep it open. A success message identifies the file, updates Last backup created, and confirms that the download started. Check your browser's Downloads to verify the file finished saving. If confirmation is delayed, check Downloads before retrying with a fresh authenticator or recovery code. Keep the file, its password, and the separate DNR 2FA encryption key securely backed up. None can be recovered from the others. Ask the deployment operator to restore records and uploaded files together; restoration is handled outside the web application.

manual-topic-administration-operations.title: Operations
manual-topic-administration-operations.text: The internal operations view summarizes task backlog, geocoding retries, inbound mail review/failures, recent authentication failures, migration readiness, and the last encrypted backup. Use it to identify operational work that needs attention before it becomes a user-facing problem. Mail Ingestion shows the latest mailbox check and import separately, plus failures and historical messages awaiting review. Ask the deployment operator to resolve a failing scan or review historical mail; use Inbox for messages already imported that need routing.

manual-topic-administration-edit-a-user-.title: Edit a User's Profile
manual-topic-administration-edit-a-user-.text: User cards group editing and security actions separately from account access and deletion. Amber Deactivate suspends access; red Delete user permanently removes an inactive or invited account. Active accounts and your own account remain protected from deletion. 01 Unlock and choose the account. Open Users, unlock sensitive actions, and select the account's Edit control. 02 Review identity and contact details. Edit the first name, last name, country-aware phone number, username, and role. Upload, replace, or remove the profile picture; JPEG, PNG, and WebP files up to 5 MB are supported. 03 Review the daily digest. Adjust notification preferences and save. A paused digest remains paused when you only change profile details. Recovery-email changes still use the account holder's separate verification flow. The updated name and portrait appear wherever that account is shown. Profile edits retain the user's authentication and recovery protections and are recorded in the audit history.

manual-topic-administration-compare-remo.title: Compare Remote Network Performance
manual-topic-administration-compare-remo.text: Administrators open Network in the sidebar to view Remote Network Performance. It compares measured page loads from signed-in public IPv4 and IPv6 clients. Choose a data window from 1 to 7 days, then select Apply. Select Refresh for current results; the page also refreshes every 30 seconds. • IPv4 and IPv6 cards: review the median page-load time, sample count, 75th percentile, median TTFB (time to first byte), and most-seen Cloudflare edge when available. Lower durations mean faster observed loads. • Contact images: compare the median duration of the slowest contact image on pages that loaded at least one contact photo. The accompanying count is the number of those pages. • Slowest Observed Pages: compare each page's IPv4 and IPv6 75th-percentile load times and sample counts. On narrow screens, each page becomes a labeled card. • Assessment: the banner highlights a material gap between the two families. Compare sample counts and page mix as well as timing; the samples come from ordinary traffic on different devices and connections. Local and private-address sessions are excluded. An empty card means no sample from that public address family has arrived; it does not establish whether the connection is healthy or broken. The server determines the family from the trusted client connection. Measurements store page names and timings without client IP addresses or user identities. Samples older than 30 days expire automatically; the dashboard shows the newest 24 hours.

manual-topic-administration-reset-networ.title: Reset Network Traffic Statistics
manual-topic-administration-reset-networ.text: 01 Choose Reset Statistics. Select the rose button beside Refresh on Remote Network Performance. If access is locked, confirm your administrator password and a fresh authenticator or recovery code, then return to Network. 02 Check the countdown and scope. The shared unlock banner shows the remaining time; use Add 5 Minutes before it expires if you need more time. Select Reset Statistics again to review the confirmation. It clears all recorded IPv4 and IPv6 samples, including page and image timings outside the 24-hour dashboard window. 03 Confirm or cancel. Select Reset Statistics in the dialog to clear the measurements, or Cancel to keep them. The reset is permanent and recorded in the audit log. QR and presentation-link statistics are preserved. 04 Watch new traffic arrive. A success message appears and the dashboard loads current results. New public page loads begin accumulating immediately, so a fresh sample may already appear. If the unlock expired, authenticate again before resetting.

manual-topic-administration-permanent-me.title: Permanent Means Permanent
manual-topic-administration-permanent-me.text: Deleting an organization preserves contacts who have another organization affiliation, and removes its remaining contacts and engagements together with their Chron, tasks, presentations, contact assignments, and financial reports. Deleting an engagement removes the same event-specific data. Deleting a contact removes that contact's Chron, tasks, and event role assignments. Active users must be deactivated before deletion; pending invitations can be deleted directly. Use archive for ordinary record retirement. Administrators can use individual Delete actions or select multiple items on the Organizations, Contacts, Speakers, Engagements, Tasks, and Users lists. Select all applies only to the current page. Review the selected names and related data, complete admin unlock when needed, and confirm the "Are you sure?" dialog. For inactive or invited users, type DELETE USER for an individual account or DELETE USERS for a batch.

manual-topic-administration-review-docum.title: Review Document and Recovery Health
manual-topic-administration-review-docum.text: Network diagnostics includes Remote Document Responses for PDF and PowerPoint activity as well as page/image measurements. Read the response and timing labels before comparing servers. Operations shows deployment and ingestion status; failures require diagnosis, not repeated submission of financial records. Browser backups include uploaded files and report capacity issues. Follow the displayed recovery instructions if the browser cannot hold the backup.

manual-topic-administration-user-lifecyc.title: User lifecycle effects
manual-topic-administration-user-lifecyc.text: Deactivating a user revokes their sessions and private calendar links and leaves their assigned work unassigned. Reactivating them does not recreate subscriptions or restore task ownership; review both explicitly. An administrator can issue a temporary password or reset another user's authenticator after fresh confirmation. The old password, authenticator secret, and recovery codes cannot be displayed. Active accounts must be deactivated before deletion. Pending invitations may be deleted directly. Account removal is distinct from archiving operational records.

manual-topic-administration-deployment-n.title: Deployment notices and recovery boundaries
manual-topic-administration-deployment-n.text: When a deployment is announced, finish or preserve your current work and follow the on-screen preparation/countdown message. Wait for service to return before retrying a save. The PDF documents browser operations. Deployment, secret management, database restoration, migration repair, and infrastructure configuration belong to the deployment operator. Use the Exact database restore runbook in README.md and docs/release-workflow.md for those procedures. The internal operations/readiness views help diagnose service state. They are not a substitute for a verified recovery backup or a successful restore check.

manual-topic-administration-understand-m.title: Understand mailbox health
manual-topic-administration-understand-m.text: Mail Ingestion separates the most recent mailbox check from the most recent new import. A current check with no new import can simply mean that no new mail arrived. A failed or overdue check, historical review backlog, or quarantined message needs operator attention. These are separate from messages already in Inbox waiting for a user to select the correct Chron logs.

manual-topic-administration-reset-and-re.title: Reset and retire an account
manual-topic-administration-reset-and-re.text: Unlock sensitive actions on Users before selecting a reset or lifecycle control. Reset User Password asks for a new temporary password and confirmation. The user must replace it at sign-in. Reset 2FA uses the explicit RESET 2FA confirmation phrase. Resetting another user's factor is an account recovery action; the old secret and recovery codes remain unavailable. Review the deactivation confirmation before proceeding. To delete an invited or inactive account, use its Delete action and the requested confirmation phrase. Do not use deletion as the ordinary way to suspend access.

manual-topic-administration-delete-inact.title: Delete inactive users individually or in a group
manual-topic-administration-delete-inact.text: On each user card, editing and security actions are grouped together; activation and deletion controls are grouped separately. Amber Deactivate suspends access. Red Delete user permanently removes the account. Active accounts and the account you are using cannot be deleted. To suspend an active account, unlock administrator actions, select Deactivate, and confirm. The current unlock countdown continues from its current deadline; it does not restart or end early. Deletion also preserves the same deadline. For one inactive or invited account, select Delete user, unlock if prompted, and type DELETE USER in the Are you sure? confirmation. Review the account name before submitting. For several accounts, select their checkboxes, choose Delete selected, and review the names. Type DELETE USERS, then select Permanently delete or press Enter to open the final Are you sure? dialog. Cancel leaves the accounts in place. Confirm only when permanent removal is intended. Active accounts and your own account have no deletion checkbox and remain protected on the server. A failed or newly protected item is kept while other eligible selections may be deleted. Read the result counts before repeating the action.

manual-topic-administration-backups-incl.title: Backups include uploaded files
manual-topic-administration-backups-incl.text: PDF Speaker Notes, PPT Slidedecks, and profile, contact, and speaker photos are saved in persistent file storage. Application records retain their metadata and associations. Uploading and replacing them uses the same forms as before. The encrypted .dnrbackup export contains both the database and the uploaded files needed by those records. Keep the whole backup together and give the deployment operator the matching backup password and separately protected 2FA encryption key when arranging recovery. Restoring an older database-only backup cannot recover files it never contained. The operator should follow the current README restore procedure and verify the restored attachments before reopening the application.

manual-topic-administration-recent-admin.title: Recent Administration and Recovery Changes
manual-topic-administration-recent-admin.text: Network diagnostics compares remote page, image, PDF and PowerPoint response measurements, with Refresh and administrator Reset Statistics. Loading or empty measurements are not proof that an upload failed. Operations shows current deployment and ingestion health. Follow the runbook if document scanning or delivery workers are unhealthy. Backups include uploaded files; the browser backup workflow detects capacity problems and gives an actionable error rather than silently producing a partial download. Keep backup encryption/recovery material secure and follow the application's restore validation. Sensitive deployment secrets are not fields in Reimbursement Setup. The deployment has bounded data/file maintenance, encryption-key rotation support, and optional private document scanning. These are operator services, not extra end-user buttons. Scanner requirements are configuration-dependent; pending/rejected required checks prevent protected file use. Local development may deliberately leave scanning disabled.

manual-topic-administration-review-users.title: Review users and access state
manual-topic-administration-review-users.text: Figure 100. Review users and access state. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Review the identity, account state, 2FA, contact details, and Daily Digest days on each card. 02 Use the lower action bar: Edit user and security controls are grouped separately from account access and deletion. 03 Amber Deactivate suspends an active account; red Delete user permanently removes an inactive or invited account after confirmation. 04 Only eligible accounts have deletion checkboxes. Individual Delete user remains available alongside Delete selected. Screenshot context: Fictional accounts illustrate active and inactive states. No account was deactivated or deleted during capture. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Troubleshooting (p. 157) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-administration-delete-one-i.title: Delete one inactive user
manual-topic-administration-delete-one-i.text: Figure 101. Delete one inactive user. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Find the inactive or invited account and select its red Delete user button. 02 Unlock administrator actions if prompted. Check that you selected the intended account. 03 Type DELETE USER exactly and select Delete user, or press Enter in the phrase field. Cancel keeps the account. Screenshot context: The confirmation is illustrated without submitting the deletion. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Troubleshooting (p. 157) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-administration-review-sever.title: Review several inactive users before deletion
manual-topic-administration-review-sever.text: Figure 102. Review several inactive users before deletion. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 On Users, select eligible account checkboxes, or use Select all on this page, then Delete selected. 02 Review the account names. Active users and your own account are protected. The selection survives an unlock redirect and expires after 30 minutes. 03 Type DELETE USERS. Select Permanently delete or press Enter to open the final confirmation. 04 Cancel returns to the user list without deleting. Changing the list page or filters starts a new selection. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Troubleshooting (p. 157) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-administration-confirm-or-c.title: Confirm or cancel the batch
manual-topic-administration-confirm-or-c.text: Figure 103. Confirm or cancel the batch. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 The Are you sure? dialog appears after the review, including when you use Enter in the confirmation field. 02 Select Delete permanently only when ready. Cancel closes the dialog without deleting accounts. 03 Read the result counts on the user list. Deletion checks administrator access and the current unlock deadline again. Screenshot context: Enter was verified to open this dialog. The batch was canceled; no accounts were deleted. manual-topic-administration-invite-a-new.text: Figure 104. Invite a new user. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Confirm administrator access, then choose a unique username, email address, and role. 02 Review the recipient and access level before sending the invitation. 03 The recipient creates their own password through the activation link. Configure digest preferences from the user editor afterward. Screenshot context: This form is shown without submitting an invitation. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Troubleshooting (p. 157) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-administration-confirm-admi.title: Confirm administrator access
manual-topic-administration-confirm-admi.text: Figure 105. Confirm administrator access. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Select Admin Unlock in the sidebar, or open a protected action. Users also provides its own unlock panel. 02 Enter your current administrator password and a fresh authenticator or unused recovery code. 03 Select Unlock Sensitive Actions to return to the requested page. The five-minute unlock applies only to this signed-in session. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Troubleshooting (p. 157) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-administration-inspect-the-.text: Figure 106. Inspect the audit trail. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Filter by category, search text, date range, and exact IP address. 02 Review actor, action, affected record, and local/UTC timestamps. 03 Individual audit records cannot be edited or removed through ordinary record controls. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Troubleshooting (p. 157) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-administration-preview-audi.text: Figure 107. Preview audit retention. manual-topic-administration-export-an-en.title: Export an encrypted backup with uploaded files
manual-topic-administration-export-an-en.text: Figure 108. Export an encrypted backup with uploaded files. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Open Database. The encrypted snapshot includes application records, PDF notes, PowerPoint files, and uploaded portraits. 02 Enter your administrator password and a fresh factor. Choose and confirm a unique backup password of at least 16 characters, then Encrypt and Download Backup. 03 Keep the page open while the export runs. Check the success message, Last backup created, and browser Downloads for completion. 04 Keep the complete .dnrbackup file, its password, and the separate 2FA key securely backed up. Ask the deployment operator to restore records and files together. Screenshot context: The credential and download section is shown with empty fields. No backup was exported during capture. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Troubleshooting (p. 157) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-administration-review-data-.title: Review data and recovery health
manual-topic-administration-review-data-.text: Figure 109. Review data and recovery health. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Administrators can inspect workload, Mail Ingestion, and Data and Recovery Health. 02 No report received means no reported result. A downloaded database backup is tracked separately; an operator must verify recovery before treating it as ready. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Troubleshooting (p. 157) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-administration-edit-a-user-.title: Edit a user's profile and digest preferences
manual-topic-administration-edit-a-user-.text: Figure 110. Edit a user's profile and digest preferences. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Unlock sensitive administrator actions, then select Edit user on the Users page. 02 Edit first/last name, country-aware phone, username, and role. Replace or remove the profile picture; JPEG, PNG, and WebP uploads allow up to 5 MB. 03 Review daily digest settings and save. Ordinary profile edits preserve a paused digest. 04 The account holder changes recovery email through the separate verification flow in My Profile. Screenshot context: The current form groups personal details together. Scroll to profile picture, username, role, digest preferences, and Save changes. No profile changes were saved. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Troubleshooting (p. 157) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-administration-choose-the-n.title: Choose the network comparison window
manual-topic-administration-choose-the-n.text: Figure 111. Choose the network comparison window. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Choose a Data Window from 1 through 7 days and select Apply. 02 Browser page-load and document-response measurements are separate. No public-client samples in this isolated preview is not evidence of a network failure. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Troubleshooting (p. 157) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-administration-extend-or-lo.title: Extend or lock administrator actions
manual-topic-administration-extend-or-lo.text: Figure 112. Extend or lock administrator actions. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Fresh confirmation begins a five-minute unlock in this signed-in session. 02 While unlocked, Add 5 Minutes extends the current deadline. Lock Admin Actions ends access immediately; expiration requires fresh confirmation. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Troubleshooting (p. 157) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-administration-reset-networ.title: Reset network traffic statistics
manual-topic-administration-reset-networ.text: Figure 113. Reset network traffic statistics. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Select the rose Reset Statistics button next to Refresh. If locked, authenticate and select Reset Statistics again after returning. 02 Review the confirmation: all recorded IPv4/IPv6 page and image timings across every date will be cleared. 03 Confirm Reset Statistics before the unlock expires, or Cancel to keep the samples. New traffic starts counting from zero; presentation QR visits are unaffected. Screenshot context: The confirmation was canceled; no statistics were reset during screenshot capture. Related chapters: Roles and access (p. 11) / Profile and security (p. 124) / Troubleshooting (p. 157) / Reimbursements (p. 105)

manual-topic-troubleshooting-troubleshoo.title: Troubleshooting and Good Practice
manual-topic-troubleshooting-troubleshoo.text: Most surprises come from role limits, archived parent records, delayed background work, or intentionally strict safety checks. Related chapters: Getting oriented (p. 4) / Engagements (p. 26) / Chron and email (p. 89) / Administration (p. 138)

manual-topic-troubleshooting-ai-coach-is.title: AI Coach Is Slow or Cannot Answer
manual-topic-troubleshooting-ai-coach-is.text: Keep the panel open or move to another MOED page in the same browser tab while the answer is being prepared. Use Stop answer if you want to cancel it. If it reports that it cannot answer, try the question again after the service recovers. The User Manual and supported guided walkthroughs remain available even when conversational answers are unavailable. A failed answer does not mean your event or file was not saved; check the application's own save confirmation. Administrators can open the request to inspect its result, duration, and failure details. If the ai coach button is absent throughout the application, ask an administrator whether the feature is enabled.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-the-coach-n.title: The Coach Names a Control I Cannot See
manual-topic-troubleshooting-the-coach-n.text: Check the page and selected tab. For example, Edit Presentations appears under the event's Presentations tab. Creating an event starts at Engagements > + New Engagement, not Organization Details. Editing also requires an editor or administrator role. Use i can't see that control on the walkthrough card to report the mismatch, or rate the answer needs work. Open its Comprehensive Manual source for the complete procedure. The coach cannot make a hidden or unauthorized control available.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-the-coach-a.title: The Coach Answer Is Wrong or Does Not Fit My Question
manual-topic-troubleshooting-the-coach-a.text: Select needs work on the answer. You can ask a follow-up describing the task you are trying to complete; a new question ends any current walkthrough. Use New conversation if the earlier discussion is no longer relevant. Feedback is recorded for investigation; it does not correct the model immediately. Follow the actual application controls and check the linked manual before making a change. You do not need to supply training material or write the corrected procedure to report a problem.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-network-sho.title: Network Shows Only IPv4 or Only IPv6
manual-topic-troubleshooting-network-sho.text: The dashboard needs signed-in public traffic from both address families. Local or private-address browsing does not add samples. Wait for public page loads, then select Refresh; a missing family alone is not evidence of a network failure. After Reset Statistics, previous samples have been cleared and new traffic must arrive.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-the-adminis.title: The Administrator Countdown Has Ended
manual-topic-troubleshooting-the-adminis.text: Unlock sensitive actions again with your password and a fresh factor. The current unlock deadline is shared by pages in your session and does not restart when you navigate. While unlocked, Add 5 Minutes extends it. Another browser session needs its own unlock.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-i-cannot-se.title: I Cannot See an Edit or Delete Button
manual-topic-troubleshooting-i-cannot-se.text: Reviewers are read only. Editors can edit and archive but cannot permanently delete. Administrators must freshly unlock sensitive access before many delete and user-management controls appear. Archived records are viewed separately and generally must be restored before editing.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-an-organiza.title: An Organization Will Not Archive
manual-topic-troubleshooting-an-organiza.text: Archive or move every active contact, engagement, and inquiry belonging to it first. MOED prevents archiving the parent while active child records would become stranded.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-search-did-.title: Search Did Not Find an Engagement
manual-topic-troubleshooting-search-did-.text: Use terms of at least three characters. Remove quotation marks to match any word; quote a group when all its words must match. Check the Archived view and the lifecycle filter. Search indexes active Chron entries, not archived ones.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-a-new-addre.title: A New Address Has No Map Pin
manual-topic-troubleshooting-a-new-addre.text: Confirm that the engagement contains a usable location and fits the current lifecycle/date filters. New addresses are processed asynchronously; keep the Map page open and the pin will appear automatically when the lookup finishes. If it remains pending, ask an administrator to check the geocoding queue and provider health.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-an-email-st.title: An Email Still Needs Review
manual-topic-troubleshooting-an-email-st.text: Confirm the sender or participant address exactly matches one active record. Correct missing contact/organization email data, preserve a single valid [DNR#ID.<signed-token>] marker in the subject or plain-text body where applicable, then choose Find matches again, or select the intended destinations and choose Save to Chron logs.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-an-outbound.title: An Outbound Email Failed or Cannot Be Queued
manual-topic-troubleshooting-an-outbound.text: Confirm that the engagement has a selected contact or a speaker assigned to an active presentation with a valid email address. Open the outbound message to see which recipient failed. Correct the address if needed, then select Retry Failed Deliveries. If sending is unavailable for every message, ask an administrator to check the mail setup.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-a-template-.title: A Template Is Missing or My Changes Cannot Be Saved
manual-topic-troubleshooting-a-template-.text: Clear the library search and check Archived. Restore a template to make it available for new emails; permanently deleted templates cannot be restored. If another session changed the template, keep a copy of your edits, reload, and compare with the current version. Use only the listed event fields with matching double braces; Presentation schedule is allowed in the message only.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-a-speaker-i.title: A Speaker Is Missing from Email Recipients
manual-topic-troubleshooting-a-speaker-i.text: Check that the speaker is assigned to an active presentation on this engagement. Add or correct their email on the speaker record, then reload the composer and select the speaker. Archived presentations do not supply recipients. Putting a speaker's name in template text does not select that person as a recipient.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-a-calendar-.title: A Calendar Stopped Refreshing
manual-topic-troubleshooting-a-calendar-.text: Check whether that device's subscription is still Active. A revoked URL cannot be recovered; create a new device-specific link and replace the old subscription in the calendar application.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-an-event-or.title: An Event or Task Is Missing from the Month Calendar
manual-topic-troubleshooting-an-event-or.text: Confirm the displayed month and selector. Events does not include tasks, My Tasks includes only work assigned to you, and task views include only active tasks with due dates. Use Everything when you want events and all due-dated work together.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-every-new-e.title: Every New Event Includes Tasks We Do Not Need
manual-topic-troubleshooting-every-new-e.text: Standard Event Tasks are a customizable starting checklist. Editors and administrators can go to Work Queue > Standard Event Tasks to adjust it to the team's workflow. Edit a standard task to change its title, notes, priority, display order, or due-date rule. Due dates can be relative to the event's start or end; for example, select Event start and enter a Day offset of -7 for seven days before the start. Use + New Standard Task to add a recurring checklist item. In the Active list, use a standard task's Archive action when it should no longer be created automatically for new events. Use Restore in the Archived tab to include it in future events again. This is the shared checklist: changes apply to everyone creating events, so agree on the team's recurring needs before changing it. If a task is unnecessary for just one event, archive that event's copy in Follow-Up Work or the Work Queue. Archiving an individual event task does not disable its standard template. Likewise, archiving a standard task does not remove copies already created on existing events; archive those copies individually when appropriate. The exception is the required built-in financial closeout reminder, due one week after the event ends. It cannot be edited, archived, or deleted.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-changing-th.title: Changing the Caller Did Not Move Existing Tasks
manual-topic-troubleshooting-changing-th.text: The Caller is used only to choose the owner of the initial standard checklist when the engagement is created. Later Caller changes do not alter existing task ownership. If responsibility changes, reassign those tasks in the Work Queue.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-a-qr-code-w.title: A QR Code Will Not Copy
manual-topic-troubleshooting-a-qr-code-w.text: Use the PNG or SVG download links to save a generated code. You can also select the QR preview to copy it; if clipboard access is unavailable, the application opens a preview. To share a web address instead of an image, use the Copy Link icon beneath the code's image. If copying is blocked, allow clipboard access for this site and retry. Save the presentation first if its QR codes are not yet available.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-a-presentat.title: A Presentation File or Its QR Code Is Missing
manual-topic-troubleshooting-a-presentat.text: Open Edit Presentations on the event's Presentations tab and check the selected speaker. Choose a PDF for Speaker Notes or a .ppt or .pptx file for PPT Slidedeck. PDF files may be up to 100 MB and PowerPoint files up to 500 MB; keep all files in one save under 600 MB total. Choosing a file or selecting Remove only prepares a change. Select Save Changes in the persistent bottom bar, then check the saved filename and upload details. The corresponding QR code appears after the file is saved successfully. Removing the file hides its code until a replacement is saved.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-a-save-repo.title: A Save Reports an Expired Request
manual-topic-troubleshooting-a-save-repo.text: Reload the page and repeat the change. MOED rejects stale or missing request tokens, and concurrent edits may require you to reopen the newest record before saving.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-i-was-signe.title: I Was Signed Out Unexpectedly
manual-topic-troubleshooting-i-was-signe.text: Password changes, password recovery, administrator resets, account changes, deactivation, and database restoration invalidate existing sessions by design. Sign in again with the current credentials or contact an administrator if the account is unavailable.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-record-the-.title: Record the Why
manual-topic-troubleshooting-record-the-.text: Chron should preserve the decision and context a future teammate needs, not just "called."

manual-topic-troubleshooting-name-the-ne.title: Name the Next Action
manual-topic-troubleshooting-name-the-ne.text: Turn commitments into tasks with an owner and date while the conversation is fresh.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-archive-bef.title: Archive Before Deleting
manual-topic-troubleshooting-archive-bef.text: Relationship history and event outcomes are usually more valuable than a perfectly tidy active list.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-protect-pri.title: Protect Private Links
manual-topic-troubleshooting-protect-pri.text: Calendar URLs, invitation links, verification links, recovery links, and recovery codes are credentials.

manual-topic-troubleshooting-search-for-.title: Search for presentation deletion
manual-topic-troubleshooting-search-for-.text: Figure 114. Search for presentation deletion. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 Search the Manual for delete a presentation. 02 Choose Archive or Delete a Presentation to jump to instructions for the buttons within each saved presentation block. Related chapters: Getting oriented (p. 4) / Engagements (p. 26) / Chron and email (p. 89) / Administration (p. 138)

manual-topic-operator-appendix-installat.title: Installation
manual-topic-operator-appendix-installat.text: To set up the project on your local machine, follow these steps: 01 Clone the repository Copy the clone URL from the repository's Code menu and replace <repository-url> below: git clone '<repository-url>' DNR 02 Navigate to the project directory cd DNR 03 Create deployment secrets cp .env.example .env install -d -m 700 secrets backups umask 077 openssl rand -hex 32 > secrets/mysql_root_password openssl rand -hex 32 > secrets/mysql_app_password openssl rand -hex 32 > secrets/mysql_backup_password openssl rand -hex 32 > secrets/mysql_maintenance_password openssl rand -hex 32 > secrets/mysql_geocoder_password openssl rand -hex 32 > secrets/mysql_mail_ingest_password openssl rand -hex 32 > secrets/mysql_mail_dispatch_password openssl rand -base64 32 > secrets/dnr_2fa_encryption_key openssl rand -base64 32 > secrets/dnr_inbound_routing_key openssl rand -hex 32 > secrets/deployment_backup_password : > secrets/backup_password chmod 600 secrets/* Store protected offline copies of dnr_2fa_encryption_key and deployment_backup_password separately from database backups. Do not rotate these keys casually: enrolled factors and encrypted deployment archives depend on them. The separate empty backup_password file is populated only for a one-shot browser-format restore and is removed afterward. 04 Build and run the application using Docker Compose # Load the images.env from the qualified release artifact first. set -a . /path/to/release/images.env set +a ./scripts/compose_with_provenance.sh production Production mode requires HTTPS from a trusted reverse proxy and uses only source code baked into the immutable image. For local HTTP development, run ./scripts/compose_with_provenance.sh development and browse to http://localhost:8080. The published port binds to 127.0.0.1 even when the production DNR_BIND_ADDRESS is configured for a LAN interface. Exposing plaintext development mode remotely requires both a non-loopback DNR_DEV_BIND_ADDRESS and DNR_DEV_ALLOW_REMOTE_HTTP=1; use that opt-in only on an explicitly trusted network, never as production ingress. A one-shot migrator applies the baseline and every forward migration before the web or worker services can start, so no separate fresh-install migration command is required. 05 Create the first administrator on a fresh database docker compose exec web dnr-create-admin admin The command securely prompts for a password. The administrator must enroll an authenticator during the first login. DNR no longer installs accounts with known default passwords. A server administrator can securely reset an existing account password from the container console: docker compose exec web dnr-set-password USERNAME

manual-topic-operator-appendix-upgrading.title: Upgrading an existing database
manual-topic-operator-appendix-upgrading.text: Follow the release and recovery workflow (docs/release-workflow.md). On s1, scripts/deploy_s1.sh pauses writers, creates and restore-verifies a fresh encrypted database backup, and only then advances the application checkout, database image and schema. Manual upgrades must enforce the same backup-before-upgrade directive (.cursor/rules/backup-before-database-upgrade.mdc). Verify the recovery copy before changing any active version; a successful dump command alone is not a restore test. For the one-time upgrade from a legacy installation that still exposes database passwords through container environment variables, run: # Production deployment (default) sh scripts/secure_existing_deployment.sh # Local development deployment DNR_COMPOSE_MODE=development sh scripts/secure_existing_deployment.sh The helper makes a timestamped database backup, generates private database credentials, writes the ignored .env with mode 600, rotates the root account and six service-specific MySQL accounts, applies tracked migrations and grants, and rebuilds the services with immutable footer provenance. An existing .env is accepted only when it has the two recognized legacy MySQL password variables. The file is never sourced: only an explicit allowlist of non-secret application settings is copied to the replacement. Deprecated password and calendar-token values are discarded. The helper refuses an already-secured, unrecognized, or partially migrated setup. This legacy credential-conversion helper is not the release deployment command. Before using it for a structural or database-version upgrade, complete the fresh, restore-verified backup procedure in the runbook; do not rely on its unverified SQL dump alone. The migration runner obtains database-administrator access only in the isolated migrator/database services. It holds a MySQL advisory lock, records applying, applied, or failed state plus each filename and SHA-256 checksum, and refuses to guess after interrupted DDL. Fresh installs and upgrades both start with migrations/20260813_baseline.sql and then follow the same ordered forward migrations. Add a new migration instead of editing an applied file. All account roles must enroll 2FA after their next successful password login before accessing application data. If the upgraded database predates password hashing and still contains plaintext user passwords, run the one-time CLI migration. It leaves recognized password hashes unchanged, invalidates sessions for migrated accounts, and requires those users to choose a new password after login: docker compose exec web php /opt/dnr/bin/migrate_passwords.php There is intentionally no browser-accessible password migration page. The audit-log and Chron-entry migrations use the database administrator account because they install triggers; MySQL requires elevated privileges for that operation when binary logging is enabled. The application continues to connect with the restricted dnruser account. The migrations record successful logins, security events, and row-level inserts, updates, and deletes for users, organizations, contacts, engagements, Chron entries, and presentations. Administrators can review this history from Users > Audit Log. Audit entries identify the actor, affected record, IP address, and UTC timestamp without storing passwords, authentication secrets, recovery codes, Chron contents, or before/after field values.

manual-topic-operator-appendix-ubuntu-24.title: Ubuntu 24.04 deployment with Proton Mail
manual-topic-operator-appendix-ubuntu-24.text: The Linux deployment is supported on the existing Ubuntu 24.04 host; it does not require an Ubuntu release upgrade. Proton Bridge runs as a non-root, headless sidecar built from Proton's checksum- verified official Debian package. Only mail-ingest shares its network namespace, so Bridge's IMAP listener remains on 127.0.0.1 and is never published to the host, LAN, or Internet. Its account, keychain, and generated credentials persist in the proton_bridge_data volume. Outbound mail should use a Proton SMTP submission token (https://proton.me/support/smtp-submission) directly at smtp.protonmail.ch:587 with STARTTLS. This keeps mail-dispatch independent of Bridge and leaves Bridge responsible only for inbound IMAP. The Ubuntu ingress also differs from the Docker Desktop deployment: it publishes no host port. Traefik and MOED share a dedicated /29 network, while Cloudflared receives one stable address on the existing proxy network. DNR trusts those exact hops. Do not replace the exact Cloudflared address with the entire shared proxy subnet; another container on that subnet could otherwise present forged Cloudflare client headers. Prepare the network and merge the tracked proxy overlay with the existing Traefik stack. Replace /path/to/traefik with that stack's directory: docker network create --driver bridge --subnet 172.29.255.0/29 moed_edge install -m 600 deploy/traefik-moed-edge.yaml \ /path/to/traefik/docker-compose.moed-edge.yml cd /path/to/traefik docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.moed-edge.yml config --quiet docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.moed-edge.yml up -d traefik cloudflared Use both Traefik Compose files for every future update to that stack. The overlay pins Traefik to 172.29.255.2 on moed_edge and Cloudflared to 172.18.0.254 on proxy; the matching defaults are already in .env.example. If either subnet conflicts on another host, change all matching values together before creating the network. Those commands preserve the current MOED host layout. For a separate deployment, merge deploy/traefik-edge.yaml instead and set the same DNR_EDGE_NETWORK, Traefik address, and Cloudflared address in both Compose projects; its defaults match the generalized Ubuntu overlay. Create the normal database/application secrets, an empty mode-600 IMAP password file, and a mode- 600 SMTP token file. Copy .env.example to .env, set the public URL and mail identities, and leave DNR_TRAEFIK_ENABLE=false during staging. Native Linux Compose mounts local secrets with their host ownership, while MOED deliberately drops the capability that would bypass file modes. Run ./scripts/prepare_linux_secrets.sh after creating or replacing any secret. It keeps the host directory private and grants read-only ACLs only to the container root and www-data identities; do not make the secret files world-readable. For Proton SMTP Submission, set: DNR_MAIL_FROM=dnr@example.org DNR_SMTP_HOST=smtp.protonmail.ch DNR_SMTP_PORT=587 DNR_SMTP_ENCRYPTION=starttls DNR_SMTP_USERNAME=dnr@example.org DNR_SMTP_PASSWORD_SECRET_FILE=./secrets/smtp_password DNR_IMAP_USERNAME= DNR_IMAP_PASSWORD_FILE=./secrets/imap_password DNR_TRAEFIK_ENABLE=false Put the SMTP token - not the Proton account password - in secrets/smtp_password. Then initialize the Bridge volume and sign in interactively: ./scripts/proton_bridge_cli.sh configure At the Bridge prompt run login, complete Proton authentication, run updates autoupdates disable, and run info. Put the generated IMAP username in DNR_IMAP_USERNAME and its generated password in secrets/imap_password; do not use the Proton account password. Exit the prompt and start the staged stack: ./scripts/compose_with_provenance.sh production-ubuntu-proton up -d --build ./scripts/proton_bridge_cli.sh status ./scripts/proton_bridge_cli.sh logs Before cutover, restore and verify the encrypted DNR backup on Ubuntu and confirm Traefik can reach the staged ingress with docker exec traefik wget -qO- http://172.29.255.3/health.php. The final cutover has two coordinated changes: remove the old moed-router and moed-service entries from Traefik's file-provider configuration, then set DNR_TRAEFIK_ENABLE=true and recreate the Ubuntu ingress service. Keeping the label disabled until that moment prevents the staged router from competing with the live Mac route. Rollback is the reverse: disable the label and restore the old file-provider route. Database initialization uses only the ordered files under migrations/. The Compose migrator service applies the minimal baseline and every forward migration, records immutable checksums and state, and then applies the single privilege manifest. There is no independent schema snapshot to drift from the upgrade path.

manual-topic-operator-appendix-deploying.title: Deploying the tracked MOED release to s1
manual-topic-operator-appendix-deploying.text: Follow Release and recovery workflow (docs/release-workflow.md) to prepare the version, merge through the six protected checks, qualify immutable images, and verify main and the release tag on both remotes. Then deploy the exact final commit: ./scripts/deploy_s1.sh "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" The command targets the configured s1 deployment and uses the complete production-ubuntu-proton-mattermost topology. It creates and restore-verifies a fresh encrypted database backup before changing the checkout, database image/schema, or application version. This is a standing deployment directive (.cursor/rules/backup-before-database-upgrade.mdc), including for manual structural/version upgrades. Configure the private s1 backup password file first (DNR_S1_BACKUP_PASSWORD_FILE, default secrets/deployment_backup_password under the deployment's project directory). Deployment holds a host lock through backup, migration and public readiness; it uses CI-qualified digests with rebuilding disabled and retains an explicit recovery record. DNR_S1_USER, DNR_S1_HOST, DNR_S1_PROJECT_DIR and DNR_S1_PUBLIC_BASE_URL can override the deployment user, host, project directory, and public URL.

manual-topic-operator-appendix-build-pro.title: Build provenance
manual-topic-operator-appendix-build-pro.text: Use scripts/compose_with_provenance.sh instead of invoking a Compose build directly. It derives the checked-out commit and UTC commit timestamp, validates both values, exports them as Docker build arguments, and then runs Compose. It refuses a dirty worktree because a footer commit would not accurately identify uncommitted source files. # Local HTTP development ./scripts/compose_with_provenance.sh development # Production behind the configured HTTPS proxy ./scripts/compose_with_provenance.sh production # Production with the inbound IMAP worker ./scripts/compose_with_provenance.sh production-mail # Local HTTP development with the inbound IMAP worker ./scripts/compose_with_provenance.sh development-mail # Production with encrypted queued SMTP delivery ./scripts/compose_with_provenance.sh production-smtp # Production SMTP with a private pinned trust anchor ./scripts/compose_with_provenance.sh production-smtp-ca # Production with both inbound IMAP and outbound SMTP workers ./scripts/compose_with_provenance.sh production-mail-smtp # Ubuntu production with private Traefik ingress and headless Proton Bridge ./scripts/compose_with_provenance.sh production-ubuntu-proton # Production IMAP and SMTP with a private pinned SMTP trust anchor ./scripts/compose_with_provenance.sh production-mail-smtp-ca # Local equivalents ./scripts/compose_with_provenance.sh development-smtp ./scripts/compose_with_provenance.sh development-smtp-ca ./scripts/compose_with_provenance.sh development-mail-smtp ./scripts/compose_with_provenance.sh development-mail-smtp-ca # Forward a specific Compose command or service selection ./scripts/compose_with_provenance.sh development up -d --build web ingress # Display the metadata without running Docker ./scripts/compose_with_provenance.sh --print-metadata For CI source archives without .git, export a complete 40-character DNR_BUILD_COMMIT and a UTC DNR_BUILD_TIMESTAMP in YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ format before invoking the wrapper. Both values must be supplied together.

manual-topic-operator-appendix-daily-ope.title: Daily operations dashboard
manual-topic-operator-appendix-daily-ope.text: The application root and completed sign-ins open Dashboard, a role-aware daily operations view. It combines active engagements in the configured upcoming window, the signed-in user's active and overdue work, event-readiness gaps, and ended events that still need a financial closeout. Readiness flags identify unconfirmed events, missing venue addresses, missing presentations, and organizations without an assigned event contact. The greeting uses the signed-in user's first name when it is available. Administrators and editors also see inbound messages awaiting routing review and quick actions for creating engagements and tasks; reviewers receive the same operational context without write controls.

manual-topic-operator-appendix-inquiry-a.title: Inquiry and booking pipeline
manual-topic-operator-appendix-inquiry-a.text: Potential events begin as first-class Inquiries instead of incomplete Engagements. The Booking Pipeline organizes active records across New, Contacted, Qualified, Awaiting Details, and Proposal Sent, with separate Booked and Declined outcomes. Each Inquiry can retain an optional Organization and primary Contact, preferred and alternate date ranges, request and location details, source, owner, priority, next action, Chron, outbound correspondence, stage history, and linked follow-up work. Declining requires a reason and remains reversible until the Inquiry is booked. Create inquiries with New Inquiry in the Booking Pipeline. Inquiry email templates cover the initial response, request for details, date options, and proposal follow-up. Messages use the existing isolated delivery worker and add a signed Inquiry reply marker; matching replies return to the active Inquiry Chron. Delivery history is visible on the Inquiry and is also recorded on the selected Contact and Organization when present. Review booking validates the required Organization, title, and preferred dates; surfaces overlapping active Engagements and qualified Inquiries; and lets the user choose which open Inquiry tasks should move. Acknowledged warnings do not become unexplained hard blocks. Conversion runs in one transaction: it creates the Engagement, assigns the primary Contact as Primary host when available, moves selected tasks, generates the standard event checklist, marks the Inquiry Booked, and preserves the Inquiry as a read-only source record linked to the new Engagement. Administrators and editors can select Archive Inquiry on a declined Inquiry or a booked Inquiry that has been converted to an Engagement. Archived inquiries leave every Booking Pipeline view and its Dashboard count. Archived Inquiries provides search, filters, export, and read-only access to the retained details, outcome, history, correspondence, tasks, and Engagement link. Restore Inquiry returns the record to its previous outcome; restore a declined inquiry before editing or reopening it. Archiving an Inquiry does not archive its Engagement or follow-up tasks.

manual-topic-operator-appendix-work-queu.title: Work queue and standard event tasks
manual-topic-operator-appendix-work-queu.text: Authenticated users can open Work Queue to review assignable follow-up work. Tasks may be general or linked to one inquiry, engagement, organization, or contact. Each task supports an owner, due date, priority, notes, and the states Open, In progress, Waiting, Completed, and Canceled. The queue provides personal, overdue, due-today, next-seven-days, waiting, unassigned, completed, and all-active views. Reviewers can inspect tasks; administrators and editors can create, edit, assign, and complete them; permanent deletion remains limited to administrators. Archiving an engagement or inquiry hides its associated tasks from active Work Queue views, counts, reminders, calendars, and digests without changing any task fields. Restoring the parent returns its Open, In progress, and Waiting tasks automatically. Completed, canceled, and individually archived tasks remain outside active work. Task history stays available, and archiving an inquiry does not affect tasks already moved to its engagement. The navigation badge and the My reminders panel summarize only the signed-in user's actionable work: overdue, due today, next seven days, and waiting tasks. Administrators and editors also see their open financial closeouts. Each count links to the matching personal queue. Users with a verified email address can enable the optional daily email version under My Profile > Notifications. Engagement, organization, and contact detail pages show their open follow-up work. Active engagements also offer an optional, idempotent standard checklist covering location, travel, presentations, materials, host reconfirmation, post-event thanks, outcome capture, and financial closeout. Every active standard item is automatically added and assigned to the creator when a new engagement is saved; re-running Add missing checklist tasks on an older engagement only adds missing active items. Open Standard event tasks from the Work Queue to add, view, or edit the reusable task content, priority, event-relative due rule, and order. Archived definitions are excluded from future checklists and may be restored; administrators can permanently delete archived definitions after fresh authentication. Editing, archiving, or deleting a definition does not rewrite tasks already generated for events. The required built-in Complete the event financial closeout task cannot be edited, archived, or deleted; it is due seven days after the event end date and directs staff to finalize giving/income, lodging, and travel received.

manual-topic-operator-appendix-task-back.title: Task-backed follow-up and recoverable drafts
manual-topic-operator-appendix-task-back.text: Inquiry next actions are linked Tasks. Editing their title, owner, due date, or status updates the pipeline summary; completing or archiving the task clears the active next action. Inquiry editing can designate another active linked task. Clearing the next-action fields removes the designation without deleting the task. Booking can carry the same task forward or resolve it with a reason. Existing active inquiry next actions are migrated into tasks and included in task totals. In either email composer, Create a Task to Review the Reply creates a waiting task assigned to the sender with a chosen follow-up date. The Tasks page and outbound message show Awaiting reply or Reply received - review needed. Reply detection requires a processed message filed to the same record, from an outbound recipient, with matching In-Reply-To or References headers. A reply never completes the task automatically; forwarded messages without those headers require manual review. Tasks supports bulk reassignment, due-date changes, and completion with a preview. Each task is checked again on Apply; changed, archived, or completed tasks are skipped and reported. Clearing a bulk due date removes dates, and manual due-date changes override checklist rescheduling. Selection buttons affect only the current page. Administrative bulk deletion retains its separate review and unlock. Engagement, inquiry, and email forms offer Save Draft, Restore Draft, and Discard Draft. Drafts are scoped to the signed-in user in this browser, expire after 30 days, and are cleared after a successful save or send. Changed record versions block automatic restoration and expose saved values for manual recovery. Uploaded files must be selected again; values from removed or newly added repeat rows are retained for manual recovery when matching controls are unavailable. Drafts do not save records or send mail, and browser storage must be available for recovery. New Contact and New Organization forms warn about likely existing records by name, email, and phone. Choose Use Existing or acknowledge that the matches are different records. The server repeats the check on Save; shared contact details do not cause automatic merging.

manual-topic-operator-appendix-event-con.title: Event contacts and roles
manual-topic-operator-appendix-event-con.text: Engagement create and edit forms can assign multiple contacts with one or more event-specific roles: Primary host, On-site contact, Billing, Travel, and Materials. Search the contact directory to add existing people, or use Add new contact repeatedly without leaving the event. New people and additional organization affiliations are saved together with the event; validation errors leave the draft available for correction. A contact can belong to several organizations, each with its own role or title.
